question: The ServiceNow platform supports a broad range of plug-and-play applications. You can select included workflows or build your own workflow. Which of the following workflows are included in the platform? **(select 3)**
explanation:
ServiceNow provides out-of-the-box IT Workflows, Employee Workflows, and Customer Workflows, which can also be tailored to organizational needs.

**Learn more:** [Power of the platform: Accelerating business outcomes across the enterprise](https://www.servicenow.com/content/dam/servicenow-assets/public/en-us/doc-type/resource-center/ebook/ebk-power-of-platform.pdf) · [Customer Workflows](https://www.servicenow.com/workflows/customer-workflows.html)

question: Access Control rules can provide access security for which of these database objects?

options.label: A
options.text: For a specific role, group, or user

options.label: B
options.text: For a specific row, column, or table

options.label: D
options.text: For a specific CMDB Configuration item

explanation:
ServiceNow Access Control List (ACL) rules secure record objects identified as tables, fields, or particular records. Since a record is a table row and a field is a table column, ACLs can protect a specific row, column, or table. [ServiceNow ACL types](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/access-control/acl-rule-types.html)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow ACL types](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/access-control/acl-rule-types.html) · [Explore Access Control Lists](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/access-control/exploring-access-control-list.html)

question: Which two methods can be used to generate an Event? **(select 2)**
explanation: ServiceNow events can be generated from a Business Rule or from a Workflow. These mechanisms can queue an event for subsequent processing by notifications, script actions, or other event handlers.

question: Which modules can be used to create a new table? (select 2)
explanation:
ServiceNow administrators create custom tables through the table-administration interface. The **Tables** module supports creating custom table records, and **Tables & Columns** is the table-administration module label that provides access to those table records. A Schema Map is for viewing relationships, and the Dictionary is primarily for managing dictionary entries rather than creating tables.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Data dictionary tables](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/c_DataDictionaryTables.html) · [ServiceNow: System dictionary](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/c_SystemDictionary.html)

question: What steps are involved in importing data by using an import set?

options.label: A
options.text: Select source file; Run automap; Transform data; Clean up target table

options.label: B
options.text: Identity source; Import transform map; Run transformer, Verify import

options.label: C
options.text: Setup LDAP; Test map; Create update set; Run import; Apply update set

options.label: D
options.text: Load the data; Create transform map; Transform data; Clean up import table

explanation: Import sets stage source records in an import table. A transform map defines the mapping from that staging table to a target table, the transform moves the records to the target, and the import-set records can then be cleaned up.

question: Which instance resource lets you access guided tours, action information, and instructions for using inputs and outputs in your flow?
explanation: The Help Panel (question-mark icon) in Flow Designer provides in-product guided tours, information about actions, and instructions for working with flow inputs and outputs.

question: Which field stores a record's unique 32-character identifier?
explanation:
ServiceNow assigns each record a unique 32-character GUID in the `sys_id` field, which serves as the record’s system identifier.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Unique record identifier (sys_id)](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_UniqueRecordIdentifier.html)

question: The Report Designer includes several sections for configuring a report. Which section is used to define the report name and the table or data source for the report?
explanation:
The **Data** section is where a report’s name and its source are set. It lets the author choose the source type and select the underlying table or data source used by the report.

**Learn more:** [Report on extended tables](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/reporting/t_AccessFieldExtendedTable.html)

question: Which tool is used to create dependencies between configuration items in the CMDB?
explanation:
The CI Relationship Editor creates and manages relationships between configuration items, including dependency relationships in the CMDB.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow CI relationship editor](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/c_RelationshipEditor.html?contentId=6fRJfBm~uEAI5wxLbM~aJQ)

question: Which of the following components does the baseline Service Catalog homepage link to?

options.label: A
options.text: Record Producers, Order Guides, and Catalog Items

options.label: B
options.text: Order Guides, Item Variables, and flows

options.label: C
options.text: Order Guides, Catalog Items, and flows

options.label: D
options.text: Record Producers, Order Guides, and Item Variables

explanation:
The baseline Service Catalog homepage provides access to catalog items, record producers, and order guides. Record producers and order guides are Service Catalog item types, while item variables are configured within catalog items and flows automate fulfillment rather than acting as catalog-homepage components. ServiceNow documents standard catalog items, record producers, and order guides as basic Service Catalog item types.

**Learn more:** [Service Catalog items](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_IntroductionToCatalogItems.html) · [Service Catalog home page](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_ViewNavSvrCat.html)

question: When importing spreadsheet data into ServiceNow, what is the initial step in the process?
explanation:
A data source must be defined first because it specifies the type and location of the external spreadsheet data. ServiceNow then loads that data into an import-set staging table before mapping or transforming it into target tables.

**Learn more:** [Importing data using import sets](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/integrate-applications/system-import-sets/c_ImportDataUsingImportSets.html) · [Integration Hub - Import](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/integrate-applications/integration-hub/integrationhub-imports.html)

question:
A Service Catalog project involves building 80 catalog items. For every catalog item, these fields must be mandatory on the forms:

- Requested for
- Requested by
- Approving manager
- Delivery instructions

All other variables will be unique to the individual catalog item. Which features would you use when designing the catalog item form?

options.label: A
options.text: Create a Variable Set Template, then apply to all of the catalog items.

options.label: B
options.text: Create one Variable Set for the four variables, then add that variable set to each of the 80 catalog items.

options.label: C
options.text: Create a Record Producer that contains the four fields; then add to the record producer related list on the Catalog Items.

options.label: D
options.text: Create a Flow Designer Action, with Variable Set Data Pill, then apply flow to all of the 80 catalog items.

options.label: E
options.text: Create an Order Guide, which includes all variables; then copy and hide variables as needed.

explanation:
A ServiceNow variable set is a reusable collection of catalog variables that can be associated with multiple catalog items. Defining the four shared mandatory variables in one variable set and adding it to each item keeps their configuration consistent and lets changes propagate to every associated catalog item.

**Learn more:** [Service catalog variable sets](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_ServiceCatalogVariableSets.html?contentId=u4FVvzq6TWmNmSZvEKmBig) · [Create a variable set and add it to an item](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/t_CreateAVariableSet.html)

question: Which roles are necessary to configure a form layout by using Table Builder? (select 2)
explanation:
The `personalize_form` role grants access to Table Builder’s Forms tab and permits form-field customization. The `admin` role has administrative access to Table Builder and platform configuration, so it can also configure form layouts.

**Learn more:** [Accessing Table Builder](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/yokohama/application-development/form-builder-glide-family-release/accessing-form-builder.html) · [Customize your form layout in Table Builder](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/form-builder-glide-family-release/customize-form-layout.html)

question: Flow Designer includes many actions. Which of the following are commonly used core actions? (select 4)
explanation:
ServiceNow Core provides reusable actions available to all flows, including actions to create a record, look up a record, request approval, and pause execution until a record condition is met. These functions correspond to Create Record, Look Up Record, Ask for Approval, and Wait for Condition.

**Learn more:** [Flow Designer actions](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/washingtondc/build-workflows/flow-actions.html) · [Ask for Approval action](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/build-workflows/workflow-studio/ask-approval-flow-designer.html?contentId=qHgJnjYCLMqf3WacMzw7bw)

question: Which item displays the list of activities, or history, on a form?
explanation:
In ServiceNow, the Activity formatter is added to a form to show the record’s activity history, including tracked updates and journal entries such as comments and work notes.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Activity formatter](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_ActivityFormatter.html)

question:
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783841181189-v1ken933.png)

An order has been submitted through the Service Catalog. As a result, two records are created in the Platform. Which two records are associated with the newly ordered item? **(select 2)**
explanation: A Service Catalog order is represented by a requested-item record in the `sc_req_item` table, and the fulfillment work for that requested item is tracked through catalog-task records in the `sc_task` table. Incident, change, and problem records are separate ITSM processes rather than the standard records used for catalog-item fulfillment.

question: Which types of scripts execute in the browser?
explanation:
ServiceNow Client Scripts run JavaScript in the client web browser in response to form events. UI Policies control form behavior and can execute scripts for client-side conditions, whereas Script Includes, Access Control scripts, and Business Rule scripts are server-side mechanisms.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Client scripts](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/scripts/client-scripts.html?contentId=gjMMiJ_KH3ChA5u6JqbTog) · [ServiceNow UI policies](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/t_CreateAUIPolicy.html)

question: Which resource can be used to view information about the tables and configuration items (CIs) related to a specific use case?

options.label: D
options.text: Common Service Data Model (CSDM) product view

explanation:
A Common Service Data Model (CSDM) product view presents product-specific CSDM use cases and identifies the associated CSDM tables and data, including relevant configuration-item information.

**Learn more:** [Enterprise Architecture and CSDM framework - Legacy](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/zurich/application-portfolio-management/apm-use-case-product-view.html)

question: On a Knowledge Base record, which tab is used to specify the users who are restricted from writing (contributing) articles to that knowledge base?
explanation:
ServiceNow Knowledge Base records use User Criteria-based access control tabs to manage read and contribute permissions. The 'Cannot Contribute' related list/tab lets administrators explicitly define users or groups who are prevented from authoring or editing articles in the knowledge base, overriding any 'Can Contribute' criteria that might otherwise grant them access.

**Learn more:** [Control access to knowledge bases - ServiceNow Docs](https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/vancouver-servicenow-platform/page/product/knowledge-management/task/kb-control-access.html)

question: A new employee is joining the IT department and must perform work assigned to the Network and Hardware groups. How would you configure their access? (select 3)

options.label: A
options.text: Add User Account to Hardware group

options.label: B
options.text: Add User Account to IT Knowledgebase

options.label: D
options.text: Add User Account to itil group

options.label: E
options.text: Add User Account to Network group

explanation:
A user account establishes the employee’s identity in the instance. Adding that account to both the Hardware and Network groups gives the employee the group memberships needed to receive and perform work assigned to those teams. In ServiceNow, group members inherit the roles and assignment-related access associated with their groups.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: The User record](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/user-administration/user.html?contentId=u25NY8e2s78Dhvmtc0PTDw) · [ServiceNow: Add a user to a group](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/user-administration/t_AddAUserToAGroup.html)

question: Which component triggers a flow after a record is created or updated?
explanation:
A record-based trigger runs a flow after a record is created or updated. ServiceNow Flow Designer defines record triggers for these record operations, while date- and application-based triggers serve different event types.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Workflow Studio architecture overview](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/build-workflows/workflow-studio/flow-designer-arch-overview.html) · [ServiceNow Workflow Studio flow trigger types](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/build-workflows/workflow-studio/flow-triggers.html)

question: Which ServiceNow resource can serve as a blueprint for mapping your IT services to ServiceNow?
explanation:
The Common Services Data Model (CSDM) is ServiceNow’s standardized framework for defining service-related terms, relationships, and CMDB data placement. It acts as a blueprint for mapping IT services on the ServiceNow platform.

**Learn more:** [What is CSDM (Common Service Data Model)?](https://www.servicenow.com/products/it-operations-management/what-is-csdm.html) · [CSDM documentation](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/common-service-data-model-csdm/csdm-landing-page.html)

question: Which components make up a filter condition? (select 3)
explanation: A filter condition compares a selected field to a value by using an operator. These three elements define what data the filter evaluates and how it evaluates it.

question: Which module in the Service Catalog application is used to create a new catalog item?
explanation:
ServiceNow creates catalog items from **Service Catalog > Catalog Definition > Maintain Items** by selecting **New** on the Maintain Items list.

**Learn more:** [Create or edit a catalog item](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/de-DE/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/t_DefineACatalogItem.html)

question: What is the sequence in which Access Controls are evaluated?

options.label: A
options.text: Field-level - most specific to most general; then Table-level - most specific to most general

options.label: B
options.text: Field-level - most general to most specific; then Row-level - most specific to most general

options.label: C
options.text: Table-level - most specific to most general; then Field-level - most specific to most general

options.label: D
options.text: Table-level - most specific to most general, then Row-level - most specific to most general

explanation: $ab

question: What is frequently used to transfer customizations from one instance to another?
explanation: ServiceNow Update Sets capture customization changes and allow them to be moved between instances for review, preview, and commit.

question: Which feature helps visualize configuration items and their relationships?
explanation: Dependency View displays configuration items and their relationships in a visual dependency map.

question: When moving a homepage or dashboard between instances, what do you need to remember?

options.label: A
options.text: Manually add them to the update set

options.label: B
options.text: They cannot be moved via update set

options.label: C
options.text: They are automatically added to the update set

options.label: D
options.text: Create a separate update set for them

explanation:
Homepages and content pages are not included in update sets by default and must be manually added by unloading them. Dashboard content must also be added to the update set so the target instance receives the referenced components. [Customizations tracked by update sets](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/system-update-sets/customizations-tracked-update-sets.html)

**Learn more:** [Customizations tracked by update sets](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/system-update-sets/customizations-tracked-update-sets.html) · [Move a Core UI dashboard with an update set](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/performance-analytics/t_MoveDashboardWithUpdateSet.html)

question: Which three tables are key to an enterprise CMDB? (select 3)
explanation:
The core CMDB data model uses the Base Configuration Item table (`cmdb`) for non-IT CIs, the Configuration Item table (`cmdb_ci`) for the basic attributes of all CIs and its IT-CI descendants, and the CI Relationship table (`cmdb_rel_ci`) to define relationships between CIs.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow CMDB schema model](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/c_ConfigurationManagementDatabase.html)

question: When you create a new notification, which items must you define? (select 3)

options.label: B
options.text: Settings for handing inactive user accounts

options.label: C
options.text: Under what conditions is the notification sent

options.label: E
options.text: What the content of the notification

explanation:
ServiceNow notification configuration requires defining the conditions that trigger delivery, the recipients, and the notification content. The standard notification form organizes these as **When to send**, **Who will receive**, and **What it will contain**.

**Learn more:** [Create an email notification — ServiceNow](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/t_CreateANotification.html?contentId=650y12ua2_GdSIzlfDV50g) · [Email and SMS notifications — ServiceNow](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_EmailNotifications.html)

question: Which access-control rule applies to all fields in the `incident` table?
explanation:
A record field ACL with the name `incident.*` matches the `incident` table and any field within it. ServiceNow documents this as the table-and-any-field wildcard pattern.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow ACL types](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/access-control/acl-rule-types.html)

question: A customer wants to use a client script to validate items on a form to ensure that the submission is sensible. Which type of client script would you recommend to meet this requirement?
explanation:
An `onSubmit()` client script executes when the form is submitted and is typically used to validate form data. It can stop an invalid submission by returning `false`.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Client scripts](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/scripts/client-scripts.html?contentId=6S3mbRkaNeuGk3PoOybSxQ)

question: Which role lets a person authorize a request while having no other platform permissions?
explanation:
The ServiceNow `approver_user` role enables approvers to modify approval requests routed to them. It contains no other roles, making it the appropriate limited approval role. [ServiceNow: Base system roles](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/user-administration/r_BaseSystemRoles.html)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Base system roles](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/user-administration/r_BaseSystemRoles.html)

question: How would you configure an Access Control to let a user with the `itil` role create Incident records?

options.label: A
options.text: Name: incident.None; Operation: create; Role: itil

options.label: B
options.text: Name: incident.Any; Operation: write; Permission: itil

options.label: C
options.text: Name: incident:*; Permission: write; Role: itil

options.label: D
options.text: Name: incident.None; Permission: create; Role: itil

explanation:
A table-level record ACL for creating Incident records uses `incident.None` as the name, `create` as the operation, and requires the `itil` role. ServiceNow’s ACL documentation specifically identifies `incident.[-- None --]` with the `create` operation as creating records in the Incident table.

**Learn more:** [Explore Access Control Lists](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/access-control/exploring-access-control-list.html) · [Configure an ACL rule](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/access-control/t_CreateAnACLRule.html)

question: What determines a user's access to knowledge bases or to a knowledge article?
explanation:
User criteria define which users can access knowledge content. They can control read and contribute access for a knowledge base and read access for individual knowledge articles.

**Learn more:** [Managing access to knowledge bases and knowledge articles](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/knowledge-management/user-access-knowledge.html) · [Control access at the knowledge article level through user criteria](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/knowledge-management/t_SelectUCArticle.html)

question: How can an administrator change a form’s layout by using Table Builder?

options.label: D
options.text: By altering the page header theme

explanation:
Table Builder lets administrators visually customize a form view by adding, arranging, and configuring form sections, including their one- or two-column layouts. [Customize your form layout in Table Builder](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/washingtondc/application-development/form-builder/customize-form-layout.html)

**Learn more:** [Customize your form layout in Table Builder](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/washingtondc/application-development/form-builder/customize-form-layout.html)

question: How can you differentiate a Base Class table from a Parent Class table?

options.label: A
options.text: Extended tables are always extended from Parent tables. Extended tables are usually extended from Base tables.

options.label: B
options.text: Extended tables can be extended from Parent tables or Base tables; but they cannot be extended from both.

options.label: C
options.text: Base Class tables always have tables extended from them. Parent tables do not have tables extended from them.

options.label: D
options.text: Base Class table is not extended from another table, Parent class tables may be extended from another table.

explanation:
A base class is a parent class that does not extend another table. A parent class may itself extend another table while also being extended by child tables.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Table extension and classes](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/table-extension-and-classes.html?contentId=tcFq_LsUEHYP0jZ1YWKwsg)

question: Which ServiceNow capability lets you deliver knowledge articles through a conversational messaging interface?
explanation: ServiceNow Virtual Agent delivers automated conversational experiences and can present relevant knowledge articles within the chat interaction.

question: Which type of script runs in the browser?
explanation: UI Policies run on the client side in the browser and can dynamically change form behavior, such as making fields mandatory, read-only, or hidden.

question: Which item would **not** appear in the History section of the Application Navigator?
explanation:
The Application Navigator History tracks recently accessed standard content such as lists and records, including records opened in forms. UI pages are non-standard interfaces and are not tracked in Navigator History.

**Learn more:** [Use the Core UI navigator](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/ui16-navigator-tasks.html)

question: How is a group defined in ServiceNow?

options.label: A
options.text: A group is one record stored in the Group Type [sys_user_group_type] table

options.label: B
options.text: A group is one record stored in the Group [sys_user_group] table

options.label: C
options.text: A group defines a set of users that share the same location

options.label: D
options.text: A group defines a set of users that share the same job title

explanation:
A ServiceNow group is represented by an individual record in the Group [sys_user_group] table. Group types are maintained separately, and a group does not require its members to share a location or job title.

**Learn more:** [Create a user group](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/user-administration/t_CreateAGroup.html)

question:
On a form, which field type has this clickable icon for viewing a preview of its associated record?

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783829333555-45vthtx9.png)
explanation:
A ServiceNow reference field stores a relationship to a record on another table. A populated reference field displays the reference icon, which opens a read-only preview of the referenced record. [ServiceNow: Reference field icon](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_ReferenceIcon.html)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow — Reference field icon](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_ReferenceIcon.html) · [ServiceNow — Reference field type](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_ReferenceField.html)

question: While viewing a long list of records, you want to quickly filter it to display only records whose **Short Description** contains `email`. How could you do this?

options.label: A
options.text: Click List Magnifier to expand column search, on Short Description, type email, click enter

options.label: B
options.text: On Search box, select text, type email, click enter

options.label: C
options.text: Click List Magnifier to expand column search, on Short Description, type *email, click enter

options.label: D
options.text: Click List Magnifier to expand column search, on Short Description, type %email, click enter

explanation: In a ServiceNow list column search, an asterisk acts as a wildcard. Entering `*email` for **Short Description** matches values containing `email`, allowing the list to be filtered to those records.

question: In what way does the Event Log differ from the Event Registry?

options.label: A
options.text: Event Log contains generated Events, the Event Registry is a table of Event definitions

options.label: B
options.text: Event Log is formatted in the Log style, the Event Registry displays different fields

options.label: C
options.text: Event Log lists Events that were triggered by integrations, the Event Registry lists the Events that were triggered during the day (24-hour period)

options.label: D
options.text: Event Log is the same as the Event Registry

explanation:
The Event Log records generated system-event instances, while the Event Registry contains the registered event definitions that the platform recognizes and can use for actions such as notifications or script actions.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Event logs](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/system-events/event-logs-2.html?contentId=Swkwgxa9EhLtEsAzwF89bQ) · [ServiceNow: Event registry](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/system-events/c_EventRegistry.html?contentId=IGEU1gAUJyDNPcQemyhdFw)

question: While viewing a record, such as an incident, how can you tell whether someone else is also actively working on the Incident? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: A notification appears asking the new user to collaborate

options.label: B
options.text: A chat bubble automatically launches, so you can collaborate

options.label: C
options.text: The Work notes list contains names of the other users

options.label: D
options.text: User presence icon shows initials of users actively viewing the record

options.label: E
options.text: An icon appears to the left of fields that have been updated by other users

explanation:
ServiceNow user presence displays the initials or avatar of users who are actively viewing the same record. It also indicates individual fields that another user has updated with an icon beside those fields, helping users recognize concurrent activity and recent changes.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow User presence](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/c_UserPresence.html)

question:
Your customer needs to update a notification so that it is sent to the Caller's Manager.

Which action fulfills this requirement?

options.label: A
options.text: On the 'Who will receive' tab on the Notification record add the Caller field, then dot walk to the Caller's Manager field to add it.

options.label: B
options.text: On the Notification record create a flow and include a notification in the flow for "All receivers".

options.label: C
options.text: On the 'Send to' tab on the Notification record, add the Caller field, then dot walk to the Caller’s Manager field to add it.

options.label: D
options.text: On the 'Send to' tab on the Notification record, set "Who will receive" to Subscribable.

explanation:
Notification recipients can be dynamically selected through **Users/groups in fields** on the **Who will receive** tab. A reference field can be dot-walked by selecting the related field; selecting `Caller → Manager` therefore sends the notification to the manager referenced on the caller’s user record.

**Learn more:** [Create an email notification](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/t_CreateANotification.html)

question: Which of the following is a correct list of changes captured in an Update Set?

options.label: A
options.text: Changes made to: tables, forms, schedules, and client scripts

options.label: B
options.text: Changes made to: tables, forms, Business Rules, and data records

options.label: C
options.text: Changes made to: tables, forms, groups, and configuration items (CIs)

options.label: D
options.text: Changes made to: table, forms, views, and fields

explanation:
Update Sets track configuration customizations to application tables and fields. Form-layout changes include the associated view information, so changes to tables, forms, views, and fields are captured. Operational data records are excluded from normal Update Set tracking. [Customizations tracked by update sets](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/system-update-sets/customizations-tracked-update-sets.html)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Customizations tracked by update sets](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/system-update-sets/customizations-tracked-update-sets.html) · [ServiceNow: Customer Updates table](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/r_CustomerUpdatesTable.html?contentId=UJYBIyWG_XE5Wip9_r34AA)

question: From the User menu, which actions may a user select? (select 3)
explanation:
The User menu provides account/session and authorized administrative controls, including logging out of ServiceNow, elevating privileged roles for the current session, and impersonating users when the required role is assigned. ServiceNow documents Elevate role and Impersonate user as User menu options; logout ends the user session.

**Learn more:** [Performing admin user functions in Next Experience](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/use-next-experience-admin-user-menu.html) · [Elevate to a privileged role](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/t_ElevateToAPrivilegedRole.html)

question: Which action sequence is used to apply an update set to an instance?
explanation:
A remote update set must be retrieved on the target instance, previewed to identify and resolve potential conflicts, and then committed. Committing applies its changes to that instance.

**Learn more:** [Retrieve an update set](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/system-update-sets/t_RetrieveAnUpdateSet.html) · [Preview a remote update set](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/system-update-sets/t_PreviewARemoteUpdateSet.html)

question: What is the initial step in the process of importing spreadsheet data into ServiceNow?
explanation:
A data source defines the spreadsheet or other external file from which ServiceNow will import data. That source is used to create and load the import set before the data is mapped and transformed.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Importing data using import sets](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/integrate-applications/system-import-sets/c_ImportDataUsingImportSets.html) · [ServiceNow: Create a data source](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/integrate-applications/system-import-sets/c_CreateNewDataSource.html)

question: Which role most commonly has access to nearly all platform features, functions, and data?
explanation:
The ServiceNow System Administrator (`admin`) role has access to all system features, functions, and data. Administrators can override access control list (ACL) rules and pass role checks, giving this role broad platform-wide privileges.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Base system roles](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/user-administration/r_BaseSystemRoles.html)

question: How is the ServiceNow platform configured so that Administrators can easily set up their instances to send an email when an upgrade finishes?

options.label: A
options.text: Administrators can update the email notification named "System Upgraded" in the System Logs module by adding the appropriate User to receive it.

options.label: B
options.text: Administrators can update the email notification named "System Upgraded" in the Notifications module by adding the appropriate User to receive it.

options.label: C
options.text: Administrators can write a Client Script to send out an email to the Administrator when an Update is complete.

options.label: D
options.text: Administrators can write a Business Rule to send out an email to the Administrator when an Update is complete.

explanation:
ServiceNow provides the baseline **System Upgraded** email notification, triggered by the `system.upgraded` event. Administrators can configure the notification’s recipients in the Notifications module, without creating custom client scripts or business rules.

**Learn more:** [Baseline email notifications](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/r_BaselineEmailNotifications.html)

question: Which of the following is a formatter? Select one.

options.label: A
options.text: A formatter allows you to configure applications on your instance

options.label: B
options.text: A formatter is a form element used to display information that is not a field in the record

options.label: C
options.text: A formatter allows you to populate fields automatically

options.label: D
options.text: A formatter is a set of conditions applied to a table to help find and work with data

explanation:
In ServiceNow, a formatter is a form element that displays information not stored as a field in the record. It can present content such as activity history, process flow, or other UI-macro-based information on a form.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Using formatters](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_Formatters.html?contentId=4YkJnIShg0jk8N6FfBhDBQ)

question: A manager needs to view a month-end snapshot of Sales performance data compared with Sales targets. Additionally, the manager needs to see those monthly figures trended over time and forecast into the future. Which capability should you recommend for this manager?

options.label: A
options.text: Scheduled Reports, a custom snapshot table, and a Trend report

options.label: C
options.text: Scheduled Reports, a custom snapshot table, and a Projection report

explanation: Performance Analytics captures performance-indicator data over time, supports comparison against targets, presents historical trends, and can forecast future performance from the collected time-series data.

question: Which tool imports data from various data sources and maps that data into ServiceNow tables?
explanation:
Import Sets enable administrators to import data from multiple data sources and map it into ServiceNow tables. Transform maps within an Import Set define the field-level relationships to target tables.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Import sets](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/integrate-applications/system-import-sets/import-sets-landing-page.html) · [ServiceNow Import sets key concepts](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/integrate-applications/system-import-sets/c_ImportSetsKeyConcepts.html)

question: The Report Designer has various sections for configuring a report. Which section lets you define grouping and the calculations to run on the data?
explanation:
The Configure section is where report grouping and aggregation settings are defined. Aggregations apply calculations such as counts, averages, sums, minimums, and maximums to report data.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Vertical and horizontal bar reports](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/reporting/c_CreateBarCharts.html) · [ServiceNow: Aggregation in reporting](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/reporting/aggregation-reporting.html)

question: Which feature lets users choose an easy way to populate the most frequently used fields for a particular table?
explanation: Templates store predefined values for commonly used fields on a table, so users can apply a template to populate those fields quickly and consistently.

question: Which modules could you use to display a list of every field on the Incident table? (select 2)
explanation:
Tables & Columns provides the table record with a searchable, sortable list of its columns. The System Dictionary contains the dictionary entries that define every table and field, so its list can be filtered to the Incident table.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Data dictionary tables](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/c_DataDictionaryTables.html)

question: A department manager asks an analyst to create some reports. Where should you recommend that the analyst begin?
explanation:
The standard ServiceNow navigation for starting a new report is **Reports > Create New**, which opens the report-creation workflow. [ServiceNow documentation: Create a report from an imported Microsoft Excel document](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/bundle/yokohama-now-intelligence/page/use/reporting/task/create-report-with-imported-data-source.html)

**Learn more:** [Create a report from an imported Microsoft Excel document](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/bundle/yokohama-now-intelligence/page/use/reporting/task/create-report-with-imported-data-source.html)

question: Which no-code method can control whether a form field is mandatory or read-only?
explanation:
ServiceNow UI Policies use UI Policy Actions to set form fields as mandatory or read-only without writing scripts.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow UI policies](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/t_CreateAUIPolicy.html)

question: When designing a flow, how do you reference data from a record within that flow?

options.label: A
options.text: Drag the table icon onto the flow definition

options.label: B
options.text: Use the condition builder to specify the desired values

options.label: C
options.text: Specify the source table on the data pill related list

options.label: D
options.text: Drag the data pill onto the flow definition

options.label: E
options.text: Add the table reference using the slush bucket

explanation:
ServiceNow Flow Designer represents available record and action data as data pills. Dragging the appropriate data pill into the flow component’s configuration references that record data for use by the flow.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Exploring flows](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/build-workflows/workflow-studio/exploring-flows.html)

question: If users want to find and assign a task to themselves in the Platform, which actions can they take from the list view to make the assignment? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Select the record using the check box, then select the Person icon

options.label: B
options.text: Select the record using the check box then select the Assign To Me UI action on the List Header

explanation: $ae

question: Which of the following concepts are related to the ServiceNow CMDB? (select 4)
explanation:
The ServiceNow CMDB is a set of connected tables and fields that stores configuration-item data, including database configuration items, and their relationships. Dependency Views visualize CI and service dependencies. CMDB data supports service processes, whereas user permissions are access-control and security mechanisms rather than a CMDB concept.

**Learn more:** [CMDB schema model](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/c_ConfigurationManagementDatabase.html) · [Dependency Views](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/dependency-views/c_BusinesssServiceManagementMaps.html)

question: When importing spreadsheet data into ServiceNow, during which step is the data written to the receiving table?
explanation:
An import set first loads spreadsheet records into a staging table. Running the transform applies the transform map and inserts the mapped records into the target, or receiving, table.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Import run details](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/integrate-applications/system-import-sets/import-run-details.html?contentId=1zWfZVTGEbUT5aXTjl9HqQ) · [ServiceNow Import sets key concepts](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/integrate-applications/system-import-sets/c_ImportSetsKeyConcepts.html)

question: Which system property must be added and set to `true` to display impersonation events in the System Log?
explanation:
The `glide.sys.log_impersonation` Boolean system property enables logging of interactive user-impersonation events. When it is set to `true`, those sessions are recorded in the System Log.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Impersonation logs](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/user-administration/c_LogImpersonations.html)

question: On a Catalog Task record, how can an administrator modify the available Priority choice options?

options.label: A
options.text: In the Context menu of the form, select Configure Options

options.label: B
options.text: Right-click the Priority Label > select Configure Lists

options.label: C
options.text: Right-click the Priority Label > select Configure Choices

options.label: D
options.text: Open the Data Dictionary > select Values

explanation:
ServiceNow choice-list values are managed through **Configure Choices** from the choice field label’s context menu. This lets an administrator add, edit, reorder, or deactivate the values available for the Priority field.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: View choice list definitions](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/t_ViewChoiceListDefinitions.html)

question: Which component of the ServiceNow infrastructure defines every table and field in the system?
explanation:
The ServiceNow System Dictionary, implemented through Dictionary Entries in the `sys_dictionary` table, defines every table and field in an instance, including field properties such as type, length, default value, and dependencies.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Data dictionary tables](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/c_DataDictionaryTables.html)

question: When moving multiple update sets at once, what might you do to facilitate the move?
explanation:
Batched update sets group completed update sets so they can be processed in bulk, avoiding omissions and incorrect processing order when moving multiple sets. [ServiceNow: Working with batched update sets](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/system-update-sets/us-hier-overview.html)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Working with batched update sets](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/system-update-sets/us-hier-overview.html)

question: In a form header, which icon would you select to access Template features?
explanation:
In the form header, template features are reached through the More options (...) menu, where "Toggle Template Bar" and other template actions appear; the ServiceNow documentation for toggling the template bar directs users to select the three-dot (•••) More options control next to Save. There is no "Stamp" icon for templates in the form header, so option C is incorrect, and the Context Menu / paper-clip options relate to other functions (additional actions and attachments respectively).

**Learn more:** [Toggle the template bar](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/bundle/yokohama-platform-administration/page/administer/form-administration/task/t_ToggleTheTemplateBar.html) · [Form header](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/bundle/yokohama-platform-user-interface/page/use/using-forms/concept/form-header-by-version.html)

question: Which type of user (persona) follows clearly defined paths and workflows in the platform and has one or more roles (for example, itil and approver_user)?
explanation: A Process User performs defined operational workflows in ServiceNow and can be assigned one or more roles, such as itil and approver_user. This distinguishes the persona from an approver-only user, whose access is generally limited to approval tasks.

question:
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1784204498651-oyc6ctv4.png)

Which path would you use to access the table configuration page from a form?

options.label: A
options.text: The Form Context menu > View > Show Table

options.label: B
options.text: The Form Context menu > View > Table

options.label: C
options.text: The Form Context menu > Configure > Dictionary

options.label: D
options.text: The Form Context menu > Configure > Table

explanation:
In ServiceNow, the **Table** option under the form context menu’s **Configure** submenu opens the configuration for the table that underlies the current form. The form context menu provides controls based on the table and the user’s access rights.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Form context menu](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/c_FormContextMenu.html?contentId=TUiSZKd3JBLoHVcE2~PFEQ)

question: Which term denotes application menus and modules that you might want to access quickly and frequently?
explanation:
A favorite is a saved navigation item for quick access to frequently used application menus and modules. ServiceNow documentation states that favorites are used to quickly find and go to most-used pages, and that an application’s modules can be added as favorites.

**Learn more:** [Use the Core UI navigator](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/ui16-navigator-tasks.html) · [Managing your favorites in Next Experience](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/managing-your-favorites.html)

question: After completing work on High Security Settings, what should you do to return to normal administrator security levels?

options.label: C
options.text: Use System Administration > Normal Security module

explanation:
High Security Settings use the separately elevated `security_admin` role for protected security changes. Ending the session clears that elevated context, so logging out and signing back in returns the user to normal administrator security levels.

**Learn more:** [Exploring High Security Settings](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/exploring-high-security-settings.html?contentId=hx7Pe_csnVs~t901WF~vgQ) · [ServiceNow CSA Study Guide](https://www.servicenow.com/community/s/cgfwn76974/attachments/cgfwn76974/training-certifications-kb/9601/1/ServiceNow_CSA_Study_Guide.pdf)

question: On the knowledge base record, which tab would you use to specify which users are not permitted to write (author) articles to the knowledge base?
explanation: Knowledge base records include separate access-control tabs for read and author permissions. The "Can Author" tab grants users the ability to create and edit articles, while the "Cannot Author" tab is specifically used to exclude designated users or groups from having authoring/write privileges, effectively blocking them from contributing content even if they might otherwise qualify through group membership. This is distinct from "Can Read"/"Cannot Read," which govern viewing permissions rather than authoring rights.

question: What is frequently used to move customizations from one instance to another?
explanation:
ServiceNow Update Sets package configuration customizations so they can be transferred between instances, such as from development through testing to production.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Update set transfers](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/system-update-sets/update-set-transfers.html)

question: What is the name of the conversational bot platform that assists users in obtaining information, making decisions, and performing common tasks?
explanation:
ServiceNow Virtual Agent is its conversational bot platform, designed to help users obtain information, make decisions, and complete common work tasks through automated conversations.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Virtual Agent](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/virtual-agent.html)

question: Access Control rules can be defined using which of the following permission requirements? (select 3)
explanation:
ServiceNow ACL rules can require a user to satisfy role, condition, and script requirements. These requirements are evaluated as part of determining whether access is granted.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Explore Access Control Lists](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/access-control/exploring-access-control-list.html) · [ServiceNow: Deny-Unless ACL](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/access-control/acl-denial-behavior.html)

question: How would you characterize the relationship between the Incident and Task tables?

options.label: A
options.text: Incident table has a one to many relationship with the Task table

options.label: B
options.text: Incident table is extended from Task table

options.label: C
options.text: Incident table is related to the Task table via the INC number

options.label: D
options.text: Incident table has a many to many relationship with the Task table

options.label: E
options.text: Incident table is a database view of the Task table

explanation: The ServiceNow Incident table extends the Task table, inheriting its fields and behavior as part of the platform’s table-extension hierarchy.

question: Which ServiceNow capability assists users in obtaining information, making decisions, and completing common work tasks through a messaging interface?
explanation:
ServiceNow Virtual Agent provides automated conversational assistance through an intelligent messaging interface and is designed to help users obtain information, make decisions, and complete common work tasks.

**Learn more:** [Exploring Virtual Agent](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/conversational-interfaces/virtual-agent/exploring-virtual-agent.html?contentId=5ABaifUBvfYGiBsXDBu6wA)

question: Which ServiceNow utility offers a modern, interactive graphical interface for visualizing configuration items and their relationships?
explanation:
Dependency View generates interactive graphical maps of configuration items (CIs) and the relationships between them, enabling visualization of dependencies in the CMDB.

**Learn more:** [View a Dependency Views map](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/4AA65edJ2a~o5pASflQppQ/kFHgvpfMOBdzNOIw_MUMlA)

question: Which action enables form personalization for the `admin` role only?

options.label: A
options.text: Navigate to sys_form_properties.list and set the property glide.ui.enable_personalize_form.admin to true.

options.label: B
options.text: Navigate to Context Menu > Configure > Form Layout and select ‘Enable Personalization’ and Enter the ‘admin’ role.

options.label: C
options.text: Navigate to Context Menu > Configure > Table and add the role ‘Admin’ in the ‘Available User’ list box.

options.label: D
options.text: Navigate to sys_properties.list find the property glide.ui.personalize_form.role and set the Value to admin.

explanation:
The `glide.ui.personalize_form.role` system property defines which roles may access form personalization. Setting its value to `admin` limits that capability to the admin role.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Form personalization](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_FormPersonalizationAdmin.html?contentId=H47G7NA1YAj_DZqXi4rHlg)

question: From a form, which options would you click to add more fields to the form? (select 2)

options.label: D
options.text: Right click on header > Add > Field

options.label: F
options.text: Right click on header > Configure > UX Dashboard

explanation:
ServiceNow supports adding fields through **Configure > Form Layout**, which controls the fields displayed on a form, and through **Configure > Form Design**, whose field navigator lets authorized users add fields to the form layout. [Form designer](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_FormDesign.html)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Form designer](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_FormDesign.html) · [ServiceNow: Configuring Incident Management](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/incident-management/incident-configuration.html?contentId=4YQ_W~d6KyL_8Icljf6YTg)

question: Which item is used to configure access to Applications and Modules?
explanation: Roles define permissions and control access to applications and modules.

question: A task worker asks how they can track any updates to records assigned to them, such as customer responses. What do you recommend?

options.label: A
options.text: On My Work list, select the Activity Stream icon to show a frame with live updates

options.label: B
options.text: Click on the eyeglass icon to expand the Monitor frame

options.label: C
options.text: Open an Agent workspace tab for each record he wants to monitor

options.label: D
options.text: Select Service Desk > My Work Dashboard

explanation:
The Activity Stream displays ongoing activity associated with a task record, allowing an assignee to monitor updates such as comments, work notes, and customer responses from the My Work list.

**Learn more:** [Track or add work order task information on a mobile device](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/field-service-management/work-order-management/view-activity-stream-fsc.html)

question:
You are demonstrating to your customer a new form you created for their new application. They want to add a field to the form. Where can you do this?

(select 2)

options.label: B
options.text: Right click on form header, select Configure > Form Layout

options.label: C
options.text: Click on context menu, select Configure > Form Designer

explanation:
ServiceNow form configuration provides two direct ways to place a field on a form: **Configure > Form Layout** and **Configure > Form Designer**. Form Layout moves available fields into the form’s selected layout, and Form Designer can create and place a new field on the form and its associated table.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Form layout](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/configure-form-layout.html) · [ServiceNow: Form designer](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_FormDesign.html)

question: Which module can you use to customize your instance’s banner image, text, and colors?
explanation:
The **System Properties > Basic Configuration UI16** module provides the Core UI settings for the banner image, page-header caption text, banner text color, header background color, and related navigation colors. [ServiceNow: Configure logo, colors, and system defaults for Core UI](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/t_ConfigureLogoColorsSysDfltsUI16.html)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Configure logo, colors, and system defaults for Core UI](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/t_ConfigureLogoColorsSysDfltsUI16.html)

question: A knowledge article must be in which of the following states to be displayed to a user?
explanation:
A published knowledge article is available to users who meet the appropriate access permissions. Draft and review states are part of the authoring and approval workflow, while retired articles are no longer normally available to users.

**Learn more:** [Knowledge article states](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/knowledge-management/knowledge-article-states.html)

question: Which of the following is used to start a flow?
explanation: A trigger initiates a flow when its defined condition or event occurs. Actions run as subsequent steps, and spokes provide reusable integration capabilities.

question: When importing data from a spreadsheet, which step determines where the incoming data columns will be written in the receiving table?
explanation: Field alignment maps each incoming spreadsheet column to its destination field in the receiving table, thereby defining where the imported values are written.

question: What is the term for any component that must be managed to deliver services?
explanation: A configuration item is any component that needs to be managed in order to deliver a service. A CMDB is the repository that records configuration items, rather than the component itself.

question: Which of the following components can a Service Catalog include?

options.label: B
options.text: Order Guides, Catalog Items, and Interceptors

options.label: C
options.text: Catalog Items, Asset Contracts, Task Surveys

options.label: D
options.text: Record Producers, Order Guides, and Catalog Items

explanation:
ServiceNow Service Catalog supports standard catalog items, record producers that create task-based records, and order guides that group multiple catalog items into one request.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Types of catalog items](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/r_ExtendedCatalogItemFunctions.html) · [ServiceNow: Record Producer](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_RecordProducer.html)

question: The testing team must be able to perform activities in the test instance as if they were members of the Service Desk group. Which role do they need to switch between user accounts without logging out and signing back in?
explanation: The `impersonator` role authorizes users to impersonate other accounts, allowing them to change the active user context within the same session.

question: What steps are required to retrieve an Update Set?

options.label: A
options.text: Verify Update Set is Complete, Retrieve, Preview, Apply

options.label: B
options.text: Verify Update Set is Complete, Test Connection, Apply

options.label: C
options.text: Verify Update Set is Complete, Test Connection, Commit

options.label: D
options.text: Verify Update Set is Complete, Retrieve, Preview, Commit

explanation:
A completed update set must be retrieved, previewed for conflicts or other issues, and committed after those issues are resolved. Committing applies the update set’s changes to the target instance.

**Learn more:** [Retrieve an update set](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/system-update-sets/t_RetrieveAnUpdateSet.html) · [Preview a remote update set](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/system-update-sets/t_PreviewARemoteUpdateSet.html)

question: Which data-consistency settings can be achieved by using a UI Policy? (select 3)

options.label: A
options.text: Setting fields to accept the data in an expected format

options.label: B
options.text: Setting fields to accept the data with ‘n’ number of characters

explanation:
UI Policy Actions can set a field’s Visible, Read only, and Mandatory properties. Therefore, they can hide fields, make fields read-only, and require fields to contain a value; they do not provide standard actions for enforcing an input format or a specified character count.

**Learn more:** [UI policies — ServiceNow documentation](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/t_CreateAUIPolicy.html)

question: In which table are groups stored?
explanation:
ServiceNow group records are stored in the `sys_user_group` table, which represents Group records.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow ChangeSuccess Scoped API reference](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/glNBsgieVJ9MunSJGk6joA/GHTKxpSjfzXafn_Md6NQMw?section=ChangeSuccessScopedAPI)

question: Which kind of ServiceNow script executes in a web browser?
explanation: ServiceNow client scripts run in the user’s web browser and are used for client-side form behavior and validation.

question:
While demonstrating their incident form to a customer, they request that the Priority values display their internal terminology: P1, P2, P3, and P4. They want this to remain consistent across all Tasks. How would you do this?

Right-click Priority and select what?
explanation:
The Priority field’s displayed values are controlled by its choice-list records. Opening the shared Task-table choice list allows the labels to be changed to P1, P2, P3, and P4 while retaining the underlying values and applying the labels across task-derived tables. ServiceNow documents **Show Choice List** as the right-click action for viewing choice-list definitions; its documentation uses the distinct **Configure Choices** action for adding or rearranging choices.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow — View choice list definitions](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/t_ViewChoiceListDefinitions.html)

question: What are some examples of UI Actions that relate to Lists? (select 4)
explanation: $aa

question: Which action helps determine which modules are visible to a user?
explanation:
ServiceNow user impersonation provides the same access as the impersonated user, including identical menus and modules, so it can be used to verify that user’s module visibility.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Impersonating users](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/user-administration/c_ImpersonateAUser.html)

question: Which action lets you personalize the layout of columns in a list?

options.label: B
options.text: Click Gear Icon > Personalize window options > Select the appropriate columns

options.label: C
options.text: Select the column to be personalized and right at the header > Choose the options to personalize

options.label: D
options.text: Select the column to be personalized > Click Edit icon (Pencil) > Choose the options to personalize

explanation:
ServiceNow personal lists are customized by selecting the Personalize List icon and choosing the columns to display and their order in the personalization window.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow documentation: Personal lists](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/c_PersonalLists.html)

question: What is a Role defined as?

options.label: B
options.text: A set of user access policies

options.label: D
options.text: A set of access control rules

explanation: A role is a collection of permissions that defines the actions an assigned user or entity is allowed to perform.

question: When transferring a homepage or dashboard between instances, what must you keep in mind?

options.label: A
options.text: Download both as PDF and XML files

options.label: B
options.text: They cannot be moved via update set

options.label: C
options.text: The Platform will automatically add them to the update set

options.label: D
options.text: Manually add them to the update set

explanation:
Homepages and content pages are not added to ServiceNow update sets by default, and dashboard content must be included in the update set or already exist in the target instance. The relevant records must therefore be manually added, such as by using the appropriate unload action.

**Learn more:** [Customizations tracked by update sets](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/system-update-sets/customizations-tracked-update-sets.html) · [Move a Core UI dashboard with an update set](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/performance-analytics/t_MoveDashboardWithUpdateSet.html)

question: Which ServiceNow utility offers a modern, interactive graphical interface for visualizing configuration items and their relationships?
explanation:
Dependency Views provides interactive graphical maps of configuration items and their relationships, enabling users to inspect CI dependencies and related services.

**Learn more:** [View a Dependency Views map](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/4AA65edJ2a~o5pASflQppQ/kFHgvpfMOBdzNOIw_MUMlA)

question: How can Workflows be moved between instances?

options.label: A
options.text: Workflows are moved using Update Sets

options.label: B
options.text: Workflows are moved using Transform Maps

options.label: C
options.text: Workflows are moved using Application Sets

options.label: D
options.text: Workflows cannot be moved between instances

explanation:
ServiceNow tracks published workflow versions in Update Sets, which can be transferred and applied on another instance along with the workflow’s relevant dependencies.

**Learn more:** [Workflow movement with update sets](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/ZUQIWHvhWUsSoHqqH5PGGw/FTwQX~gjeR_YM4ledKaVdQ?section=c_WorkflowMovementWithUpdateSets)

question: Within a Knowledge Base record, where can an administrator locate the User Criteria that specify who can read the articles?
explanation:
The **Can Read** user-criteria setting controls read access to articles in a knowledge base. ServiceNow documents that read access determines users’ ability to view knowledge articles and identifies **Can Read** as the relevant access control.

**Learn more:** [Managing access to knowledge bases and knowledge articles](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/knowledge-management/user-access-knowledge.html) · [Control access at the knowledge base level through user criteria](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/knowledge-management/t_SelectUserCriteria.html)

question: How do you navigate to a table’s Schema Map?

options.label: A
options.text: System Definition > Tables; Select Table; Go to Related links and click Show Schema Map

options.label: B
options.text: System Dictionary > Show Schema Map; Select Table

options.label: C
options.text: System Definition > Show Schema Map; Select Table

options.label: D
options.text: System Definition > Dictionary; Select Table; Go to Related links and click Show Schema Map

explanation:
A table’s Schema Map is opened from the selected table record: navigate to **System Definition > Tables**, select the table, and click the **Show Schema Map** related link.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Data dictionary tables](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/c_DataDictionaryTables.html)

question: Table Access Control rules are evaluated in the following sequence:

options.label: A
options.text: any table name (wildcard), parent table name, table name

options.label: B
options.text: table name, parent table name, any table name (wildcard)

options.label: C
options.text: parent table name, table name, any table name (wildcard)

options.label: D
options.text: any table name (wildcard), table name, parent table name

explanation:
ServiceNow processes table ACL rules from most specific to least specific: it matches the table name first, then the parent table name, and finally any table name by using the wildcard (`*`).

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow ACL types](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/access-control/acl-rule-types.html)

question: Which feature ensures data consistency when importing data through import sets and web services?
explanation:
A Data Policy enforces data requirements independently of the user interface. Its settings can apply to data brought in through import sets, including web service import sets, and through SOAP web services, ensuring that imported records meet the defined consistency rules.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Data policy fields](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/washingtondc/platform-administration/r_DataPolicyFields.html) · [ServiceNow Convert a UI policy to a data policy](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/t_ConvertAUIPolicyToADataPolicy.html)

question: A customer wants to create a new template that notifies users affected by network outages at their site. Which module should you use to create a new notification?
explanation:
ServiceNow creates email notifications from the **System Notification > Email > Notifications** module. From there, selecting **New** opens the notification record where the trigger, recipients, and message content can be configured.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Create an email notification](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/t_CreateANotification.html)

question: A customer requires the ability to monitor which users perform impersonations in their instance. What should you do to satisfy this requirement?

options.label: A
options.text: Add the role Log Write [sn_log_write] to the Impersonator Group

options.label: B
options.text: Create user update set for impersonation tracking

options.label: D
options.text: From User icon, select Elevate Roles

options.label: E
options.text: On the Impersonator role record, right click and select Create Log

explanation:
Setting the `glide.sys.log_impersonation` system property to `true` enables logging for interactive impersonation sessions, recording them in the system log so the users performing impersonations can be monitored.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Impersonation logs](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/user-administration/c_LogImpersonations.html) · [ServiceNow: Log user impersonation](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/instance-security-hardening-settings/sc-log-user-impersonation.html)

question: What enables the creation of a task-based record from the Service Catalog?
explanation:
A record producer is a Service Catalog item type that lets end users create task-based records, such as incident records, directly from the catalog rather than creating a requested item.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Record Producer](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_RecordProducer.html)

question: Which characteristic applies when importing data into ServiceNow?

options.label: A
options.text: An existing Transform Map can be used one time on the same import set

options.label: B
options.text: Coalesce fields are used only after running Transform

options.label: C
options.text: Any user can manage and set up import sets

options.label: D
options.text: An existing Transform Map can be used multiple times on the same import set

explanation:
An existing Transform Map can be executed multiple times on the same import set. ServiceNow supports running selected transform maps against the same import-set data in the specified order.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Transform maps](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/integrate-applications/system-import-sets/c_CreatingNewTransformMaps.html)

question: Which import utility should you use when the field names in the import set match the names of the fields on the target table?
explanation:
ServiceNow’s Automatic Mapping Utility automatically matches import-set fields with target-table fields when their names align, using **Auto map matching fields**. Mapping Assist is intended for adjustments or more complex source-to-target mappings.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Mapping options](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/en-US/bundle/zurich-integrate-applications/page/script/server-scripting/concept/c_MappingOptions.html)

question: When managing tags, you can control who can view them. What visibility options are available? (select 3)
explanation:
ServiceNow tags can be private to the owner (**Me**), shared with specified **Groups and Users**, or globally visible to **Everyone**. Administrative roles may be required to create globally visible tags, but they are not themselves visibility settings.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Docs: Tags](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/c_Tags.html)

question: When using the Data Pill Picker, which keys do you use to dot-walk to fields in other tables?
explanation:
In the Data Pill Picker, arrow navigation opens a referenced record and exposes its fields in the related table, enabling dot-walking.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Developers: Selecting Data Pills with Data Pill Picker Buttons](https://developer.servicenow.com/print_page.do?category=learning-plans&identifier=new_to_servicenow&module=learning+plan&release=yokohama)

question: What outcome results from the order in which access controls are evaluated?

options.label: A
options.text: Ensures user has access to the fields in a table, before considering their access to the table

options.label: B
options.text: Ensures user can get to work as quickly as possible

options.label: C
options.text: Ensures user has access to the application, before evaluating access to a module within the application

options.label: D
options.text: Ensures user has access to a table, before evaluating access to a field in the table

explanation:
ServiceNow requires a user to pass a table ACL before it evaluates the field ACLs. Failing the table ACL prevents access to any fields in that table.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow ACL types](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/access-control/acl-rule-types.html)

question: Which tool defines the relationships between fields in an import set table and those in a target table?
explanation:
A Transform Map is a set of field maps that defines the relationships between fields in an import set table and fields in an existing target table.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Transform maps](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/integrate-applications/system-import-sets/c_CreatingNewTransformMaps.html) · [ServiceNow: Import sets key concepts](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/integrate-applications/system-import-sets/c_ImportSetsKeyConcepts.html)

question: Which of the following are valid ServiceNow user-authentication methods? (select 3)
explanation:
ServiceNow supports native local database authentication, LDAP integration for user authentication, and single sign-on (SSO). XML feeds and FTP authentication are not ServiceNow user-authentication methods.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Authentication](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/authentication/c_Authentication.html) · [ServiceNow LDAP integration](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/ldap-integration/c_LDAPIntegration.html)

question: What is the name of the table relationship in which two or more tables have a bidirectional relationship, allowing related records to be visible from both tables in a related list?
explanation:
A many-to-many relationship creates a bidirectional association between tables, enabling related records to appear in related lists from either table. It is implemented through an intermediate relationship table that references both tables.

**Learn more:** [Create a many-to-many table relationship](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/t_CreateAManyToManyRelationship.html)

question: Which module do you use to access the reports available to you?
explanation:
In ServiceNow Core UI, **Reports > View / Run** opens the Reports list, where users can view and run reports they are permitted to access.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: View the Reports list](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/washingtondc/now-intelligence/reporting/r_ViewTheReportsList.html) · [ServiceNow: View a report](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/zurich/now-intelligence/reporting/t_RunAReport.html)

question: How is a user defined in ServiceNow?

options.label: A
options.text: A user is a record stored in the Profile [sys_user_profile] table

options.label: B
options.text: A user is a record stored in the User [sys_user] table

options.label: C
options.text: A user is a record stored in the User Preference [sys_user_preference] table

options.label: D
options.text: A user is a field in the LDAP integration

explanation: A ServiceNow user is represented by a record in the User [sys_user] table, which stores the primary account and identity information.

question: Which instance resource lets you access guided tours, information about actions, and instructions for using inputs and outputs in your flow?
explanation:
The Help Panel, accessed through the question-mark icon, provides guided tours and contextual action help, including guidance on using an action’s inputs and outputs in a flow.

**Learn more:** [Use the help panel](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/build-workflows/workflow-studio/use-flow-designer-help-panel.html)

question: Which field or fields are used as a unique key when importing data?
explanation:
Coalesce fields are used to match import-set rows to existing target-table records. A target field configured to coalesce is treated as a unique key; a match updates the existing record, while no match creates a new one.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Create a field map](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/integrate-applications/system-import-sets/t_CreatingAFieldMap.html)

question: Which element enables administrators to add information to a form that is outside the record’s existing fields?

options.label: A
options.text: By modifying the layout to two columns

options.label: C
options.text: By dragging fields from the form elements panel

options.label: D
options.text: By adding formatters to a form

explanation:
In ServiceNow, a formatter is a form element used to display information that is not a field on the record, including content supplied through macros or scripted UI elements.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Using formatters](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_Formatters.html)
