question: Which banner icon is used to modify your personal system settings, such as the color scheme for your instance?
explanation: Personal system settings, including an instance color scheme, are accessed through the Settings icon, represented by a gear.

question: Typically, based on best practice, which of the following interactions is used to make fields mandatory, read-only, and/or hidden?
explanation:
ServiceNow UI Policies dynamically control field behavior on forms, including mandatory status, read-only status, and visibility. ServiceNow recommends using UI Policies where possible for these standard changes rather than client scripting.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow UI policies](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/zurich/platform-administration/t_CreateAUIPolicy.html)

question: What is the platform table name of the Group table?
explanation:
ServiceNow stores group records in the `sys_user_group` table.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Community: User and Group table names](https://www.servicenow.com/community/creator-studio-forum/what-is-the-user-and-table-name-for-user-table/m-p/3493023)

question: Which of the following is used to classify, flag, and find records?
explanation: Tags are labels attached to records that support categorization, visual flagging, and later retrieval.

question: When importing data, what happens to imported rows when no coalesce field is specified?

options.label: A
options.text: All rows are rejected from the import, as coalesce field is required.

options.label: B
options.text: All rows are treated as new records. No existing records are updated.

options.label: C
options.text: Duplicate rows are rejected from the import.

options.label: D
options.text: All rows are treated as new records, but errors will be flagged in the import log.

explanation:
A coalesce field identifies existing target-table records to update during an import. When no coalesce field is defined, every imported row is treated as a new record and no existing records are updated.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Updating records using coalesce](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/integrate-applications/system-import-sets/c_ImportSetCoalesce.html)

question: Which of the following are benefits of using Flow Designer? (select 3)
explanation:
Flow Designer lets process owners automate work with reusable components without writing code, reducing manual scripting and replacing complex custom scripts with upgrade-safe platform logic. Reusable actions reduce development and upgrade costs, helping reduce technical debt. Integration Hub and spokes enable flows to connect with external and third-party systems.

**Learn more:** [Flow Designer](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/washingtondc/build-workflows/flow-designer.html) · [Exploring Flow Designer](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/washingtondc/build-workflows/exploring-flow-designer.html)

question: You are viewing a list of Active Incidents and want to exclude Incidents whose state is Resolved. How could you do this?

options.label: A
options.text: On Search, select State, type not Resolved, press enter

options.label: B
options.text: On State column title, right-click, select Filter Out > Resolved

options.label: C
options.text: On the list of records, locate and right-click on the Resolved value, select Filter Out

options.label: D
options.text: On the list of records, locate and right-click on the Resolved value, select Exclude

options.label: E
options.text: Click Funnel icon, click AND, Select Resolved, is Not, State, click Run

explanation:
In a ServiceNow list, right-clicking a field value and selecting **Filter Out** adds a condition that excludes records with that value. Filtering out the Resolved value in the State field adds a `State != Resolved` condition.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Quick filters](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/c_QuickFilters.html)

question: Which capability enables users to build dashboards with widgets that visualize data over time to identify areas for improvement?
explanation: Performance Analytics provides KPI dashboards and widgets that track and visualize historical trends over time, enabling users to identify areas that need improvement.

question: What must be specified when creating a Business Rule? (select 4)
explanation:
Creating a Business Rule requires specifying the Table it runs against, the Application scope it belongs to, and what it does when triggered — either by setting field values through the Actions/'Fields to update' section or by writing a Script when the Advanced option is enabled — since these are the core components ServiceNow's platform administration documentation identifies as necessary to define a working Business Rule.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Documentation — Business rules](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/csh?topicname=c_BusinessRules.html&version=latest)

question: Which practices are recommended for users, groups, and roles? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: You should never assign roles to groups.

options.label: B
options.text: You should assign roles to users.

options.label: C
options.text: You should add users to groups.

options.label: D
options.text: You should assign roles to groups.

explanation: In role-based access control, users should be placed in groups, and roles should be assigned to groups. Group-based role assignment provides consistent permissions for members and reduces the administrative overhead and error risk of assigning roles directly to individual users.

question: Which technique is used to retrieve information through a series of referenced fields across different tables?
explanation:
Dot-walking accesses fields on related records by traversing reference fields through a dot-separated chain, including across multiple referenced tables.

**Learn more:** [Dot-walking to data in related tables](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/c_DotWalking.html)

question: What is a schema map?

options.label: A
options.text: A schema map enables administrators to define records from specific tables as trouble sources for Configuration Items

options.label: B
options.text: A schema map graphically organizes the visual task boards for the CMDB

options.label: C
options.text: A schema map graphically displays the Configuration Items that support a business service

options.label: D
options.text: A schema map displays the details of tables and their relationships in a visual manner, allowing administrators to view and easily access different parts of the database schema

explanation:
A ServiceNow schema map visually displays database tables and their relationships, enabling administrators to view and navigate different parts of the database schema.

**Learn more:** [Viewing table references and extensions](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/c_SchemaMapForTables.html)

question: What steps are used to apply an update set to an instance?
explanation:
A ServiceNow update set is retrieved from the source instance, previewed to detect and resolve conflicts, and then committed to apply its changes on the target instance.

**Learn more:** [Preview a remote update set](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/system-update-sets/t_PreviewARemoteUpdateSet.html) · [Commit an update set](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/system-update-sets/t_CommitAnUpdateSet.html)

question:
You are creating a catalog item to order a new desktop computer. The computers offer these options:

- Color: Black or Silver
- RAM: 32 MB or 64MB
- Keyboard: Standard or Ergonomic
- Monitor: 24 inch or 32 inch

How would you add these options to the catalog item form?
explanation: ServiceNow catalog items use variables to collect requester-provided options on the item form. Each hardware attribute can be configured as a variable, commonly using a choice-type variable for its available values.

question: In which area of a ServiceNow instance can you find the option to open applications such as Incident Management?
explanation: The Application Navigator is the ServiceNow navigation area used to browse and open applications and their modules, including Incident Management.

question: An IT user contacts the service desk because they need to work with task records. When they log in to the ServiceNow instance, their homepage shows only Self Service. What issue could account for this? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Their user account does not have itil role

options.label: B
options.text: Their user account was not approved by their manager

options.label: C
options.text: Their user account is not logged in properly

options.label: D
options.text: Their user account failed LDAP authentication

options.label: E
options.text: Their user account does not belong to any groups, which contain the itil role

explanation: Task-record access and the associated ITIL application modules require the `itil` role. The role may be assigned directly to a user account or inherited through membership in a group that contains the role; without either assignment, the user may have only Self Service access.

question: In which part of the ServiceNow instance can you find the **Impersonate User** option?
explanation:
The **Impersonate User** command is accessed through the user menu in the banner frame, opened from the user profile picture.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Impersonate a user](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/user-administration/t_ImpersonateAUserInUI16.html)

question: Which of the following lets a user edit field values in a list without opening the form?
explanation:
The ServiceNow List Editor supports editing field values directly from a list without navigating to or opening a form.

**Learn more:** [Use the list editor](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/t_UseTheListEditor.html)

question: What helps define the structure of a catalog item form displayed to the customer?
explanation:
Service catalog variables define the questions and input controls shown to a customer, including their types and placement on a catalog item form. ServiceNow states that variables help define the structure of the catalog item form displayed to the customer.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Service catalog variables](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_ServiceCatalogVariables.html)

question: Which of the following statements is correct about Column Context Menus?

options.label: A
options.text: It displays actions such as creating quick reports, configuring the list, and exporting data

options.label: B
options.text: It displays actions related to filtering options, assigning tags, and search

options.label: C
options.text: It displays actions related to viewing and filtering the entire list

options.label: D
options.text: It displays actions such as view form, view related task, and add relationship

explanation:
The Column Context Menu is opened by right-clicking a column heading and provides column-oriented actions: sorting, grouping, creating quick reports (Bar Chart/Pie Chart), configuring the list, and exporting data. That matches statement A. Option D describes a form/related-list menu, while options B and C describe entire-list or search/tag behaviors rather than the column heading menu. A ServiceNow community thread with a screenshot confirms that right-clicking a column label exposes quick-report, list-configuration, and export options, validating A.

**Learn more:** [About Column Context Menus](https://www.servicenow.com/community/app-engine-forum/about-column-context-menus/td-p/3497981) · [List vs Column context menu](https://www.servicenow.com/community/developer-forum/list-context-menu-and-column-context-menu/m-p/3422223)

question: A manager reports that they cannot obtain the data needed in a report because it resides in two distinct tables. The data is needed for many different reports in their department. You have verified that dot-walking cannot meet the requirement. What else could you try to help this manager?
explanation:
A ServiceNow database view joins two or more tables into a single reportable pseudo-table, allowing reports to use fields from the joined tables. It is appropriate when the same cross-table data is needed repeatedly and dot-walking cannot provide the required fields.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Joining tables using database views](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/c_CreatingDatabaseViews.html) · [ServiceNow: Working with database views for reporting](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/c_DatabaseViews.html)

question: Which type of table has a name that begins with `u_` or `x_`?
explanation:
ServiceNow custom tables are named with the `u_` prefix in the global application scope or the `x_` prefix in a scoped application. [Delete a custom table](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/t_DeleteACustomTable.html)

**Learn more:** [Delete a custom table](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/t_DeleteACustomTable.html)

question: When searching with the App Navigator search field, what can be returned? (select 4)
explanation:
The Application Navigator filter searches application names, module names and favorites, so 'Names of Applications and Modules', 'Names of Modules', 'Names of Applications' and 'Favorites' can all be returned. Matching favorites are listed at the top of the results. History records and dashboard gauge titles are not returned by the navigator filter.

**Learn more:** [Core UI application navigator – ServiceNow Docs](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/c_UI16ApplicationNavigator.html)

question: Which of the following can be configured through the **Basic Configuration UI16** module? (select 3)
explanation:
The Basic Configuration UI16 module provides system properties for the UI16 banner image, the text shown in the browser tab, and the system date format. Record number formats and form header sizing are configured elsewhere.

**Learn more:** [Configure logo, colors, and system defaults for Core UI](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/de-DE/platform-user-interface/t_ConfigureLogoColorsSysDfltsUI16.html)

question: What is the purpose of an application scope?

options.label: A
options.text: Scope determines which parts of an application are available for use by other applications In ServiceNow

options.label: B
options.text: Scope prevents applications from changing their own tables and business logic

options.label: C
options.text: Scope determines the functionality of core services in the platform

options.label: D
options.text: Scope determines all applications access each other's tables and business logic

explanation:
An application scope defines which resources of an application are available to other applications in ServiceNow, helping isolate application data and logic and prevent unintended cross-scope access.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Application scope](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/c_ApplicationScope.html)

question: Which module should you use to create a new automation for business logic, such as approvals, tasks, and notifications?
explanation:
ServiceNow Flow Designer creates flows that automate approvals, tasks, notifications, and record operations without code.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Flow Designer](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/flow-designer.html?contentId=rZaEg_PjkgH~nzf8rXjB9g)

question: What is created from the Service Catalog after a user orders an item or service?
explanation:
Ordering from the ServiceNow Service Catalog generates a request to track the order. Each catalog item within that request can also create a separate requested-item record.

**Learn more:** [Service Catalog request screens](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_RequestingAServiceCatalogItem.html)

question: Which are examples of Core tables in the ServiceNow platform?
explanation:
User, Task, and Incident are core ServiceNow tables. The Task table is a core base-system table, and Incident is a table that extends Task; ServiceNow documentation also identifies User as the table referenced by Incident records.

**Learn more:** [Working with the Task table](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/c_TaskTable.html) · [Table relationships](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/table-relationships.html)

question: Which attributes of a field can a UI Policy Action modify on a form? (select 3)
explanation:
A ServiceNow UI Policy Action can set a field’s mandatory state, visibility state (show or hide), and read-only state. Field length and format are not UI Policy Action attributes.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Using UI policies](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/zurich/platform-administration/t_CreateAUIPolicy.html)

question: If a user is on an Incident form and receives an alert after changing the value of the Priority field, which type of script runs in the Platform?
explanation: A client script runs in the user’s browser and can respond to form interactions such as a change to the Priority field, including displaying an alert.

question: Which role is able to manage multiple knowledge bases?
explanation: The `knowledge_admin` role is the ServiceNow Knowledge Management administrator role and can administer multiple knowledge bases.

question: Which part of a table holds one piece of data for a single record?
explanation: A field represents one attribute or data value within a record in a table.

question: What is a Related List used for?

options.label: B
options.text: To dot-walk to a core table

explanation:
A ServiceNow related list appears on a form and displays records from tables that are related to the current record.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Documentation: Related lists](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/c_RelatedLists.html)

question: From a related list, what would a user select to personalize the column layout?
explanation: A gear icon opens settings and personalization controls for a related list, including configuration of which columns are displayed and their layout.

question: An order for new office equipment was placed through the Service Catalog. How would you view the request lists after the orders have been submitted?

options.label: B
options.text: In the Navigation Filter, type “requests.list" and press the Enter key

options.label: D
options.text: All > Service Catalog > Open Records > Items

explanation:
ServiceNow exposes submitted catalog request items through **All > Service Catalog > Open Records > Items**. Catalog orders create tracked requests and discrete requested-item records, and the Items module opens the list of those ordered items.

**Learn more:** [Transfer a request to another department](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/fr-FR/it-service-management/request-management/req-transfer-ur.html?contentId=P4nsmGgWIAy1D2S28eTskQ) · [Service Catalog request screens](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_RequestingAServiceCatalogItem.html)

question: What protects applications by limiting access to data in another application within the same instance?
explanation:
ServiceNow application scoping protects an application's files and data from access by other applications unless that access is explicitly permitted. This is cross-scope protection, distinct from access control rules that govern user access to records and tables.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Application scope](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/c_ApplicationScope.html) · [ServiceNow: Application access settings](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/c_ApplicationAccessSettings.html)

question: What would you do on a list to display records in groups based on the **Category** column? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: On list Context Menu, select Group By > Category

options.label: B
options.text: On the Filter Menu, select Group By > Category

options.label: C
options.text: Click Group On icon, select Category

options.label: D
options.text: On Navigator Filter, type tablename.group.category and press enter

options.label: E
options.text: On the Category column title, click Context menu > Group By Category

explanation:
ServiceNow groups list records by a selected field. You can select **Group By** from the list title bar’s context menu and choose the field, or right-click the relevant column name and select **Group By**. Selecting **Category** through either method groups the list by category.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow — Grouped lists](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/c_GroupedLists.html)

question: Where should an administrator go to add the **Save** button to the form header?

options.label: B
options.text: All > System Properties > UI Action Settings

explanation:
Whether the Save button appears in the form header is a platform-wide UI setting, not part of a form's layout. An administrator turns it on under All > System Properties > UI Properties. That setting shows the extra save actions, such as Save and Insert and Stay, as buttons in the form header. Otherwise users reach these actions from the form context menu. Form designer and Form Layout only arrange the form body: fields, sections, annotations, formatters and related lists. They do not add header buttons. Form buttons themselves are UI actions, and System Properties has no 'UI Action Settings' page.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Form context menu](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/c_FormContextMenu.html) · [ServiceNow: Form designer](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_FormDesign.html)

question: Which role or roles are necessary to impersonate a user? (select 2)
explanation:
In ServiceNow, the `impersonator` role allows a user to impersonate users, but it does not permit impersonation of admin users. Users with the `admin` role can impersonate users, including for administrative testing and troubleshooting scenarios.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Impersonate a user](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/user-administration/t_ImpersonateAUserInUI16.html) · [ServiceNow: Base system roles](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/user-administration/r_BaseSystemRoles.html)

question: Which action can be performed by selecting the **Additional actions** menu in Table Builder?
explanation:
In Table Builder, the Additional actions menu lets an administrator perform table-level operations, including creating a database index on the table. Scheduling a job, duplicating a form view, and adding a module are handled elsewhere in the platform and are not offered from Table Builder's Additional actions menu, so option D is correct.

**Learn more:** [Create a table index](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/bundle/zurich-platform-administration/page/administer/table-administration/task/t_CreateCustomIndex.html) · [Table Builder](https://store.servicenow.com/store/app/981d27a21b646a50a85b16db234bcbc9)

question: Which set of permissions controls access to applications and modules?
explanation: ServiceNow roles determine which applications and modules a user can access. Access control rules regulate permissions for specific data and operations rather than application or module visibility.

question: How can fields be visually rearranged within a form view in Table Builder?

options.label: C
options.text: By dragging fields into the form editor

explanation:
Table Builder’s form editor supports drag-and-drop placement, allowing fields to be moved to the desired location within a form layout.

**Learn more:** [Add fields to a form layout in Table Builder](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/form-builder-glide-family-release/add-form-fields.html)

question: Which field type lets you look up values from one other table?
explanation: A reference field links a record to a record in another table, enabling values to be selected from that referenced table.

question: What steps are required to apply an update set retrieved from a different instance?

options.label: A
options.text: Load the Update Set > Import the Update Set > Install

options.label: B
options.text: Verity Update Set is Complete, Retrieve, Preview, Commit

options.label: C
options.text: Verify Update Set is Complete, Test Connection, Apply

options.label: D
options.text: Import the Update Set > Verify the Update Set is complete > Link the Update Set > Publish

explanation:
A source update set must be complete before another instance can retrieve it. The target instance retrieves the set, previews it to detect and resolve conflicts, and commits it to apply the changes. [Retrieve an update set](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/system-update-sets/t_RetrieveAnUpdateSet.html) and [Preview a remote update set](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/system-update-sets/t_PreviewARemoteUpdateSet.html) document this workflow.

**Learn more:** [Retrieve an update set](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/system-update-sets/t_RetrieveAnUpdateSet.html) · [Preview a remote update set](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/system-update-sets/t_PreviewARemoteUpdateSet.html)

question: What is the purpose of user impersonation?
explanation:
User impersonation enables an administrator to experience the instance as another user, with that user’s permissions and preferences, making it useful for testing and troubleshooting visibility into the user experience.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Impersonating users](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/user-administration/c_ImpersonateAUser.html) · [ServiceNow: Monitoring user activity](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/platform-administration/user-administration/user-admin-tools-landing.html)

question: What does a sys_id represent?

options.label: A
options.text: Unique 32-character identifier that is assigned to every record

options.label: D
options.text: Unique 64-character identifier that is assigned to every record

explanation:
A ServiceNow sys_id is a unique 32-character GUID assigned to identify each record in an instance.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Unique record identifier (sys_id)](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_UniqueRecordIdentifier.html)

question: What governs the process for publishing and retiring knowledge articles?
explanation:
Publishing and retiring knowledge articles is governed by Workflows (D) assigned at the Knowledge Base level. ServiceNow ships standard options such as 'Knowledge - Approval Publish', 'Knowledge - Instant Publish', and 'Knowledge - Instant Retire', and each knowledge base can use a default or custom workflow to control its publish/retire process. 'State Lifecycle' (E) is not the mechanism that drives these transitions, so the existing answer is incorrect.

**Learn more:** [Knowledge Base Workflows](https://therockethq.gitbooks.io/servicenow1/content/index/index/fundamentals/fundamentals-concepts/knowledge-management/knowledge-base-workflows.html) · [Who can retire and publish a knowledge article](https://www.servicenow.com/community/developer-blog/servicenow-learning-130-who-can-quot-retire-quot-and-quot/ba-p/2776591)

question: What must you do before using an Application-based trigger in your flow?

options.label: C
options.text: Activate application spoke, and plug-ins as needed

options.label: D
options.text: Assign Application trigger role [sn_app_trigger_write] to SME

explanation: An Application-based trigger is made available through its application spoke. The applicable application spoke—and any plug-ins it requires—must be activated before the trigger can be used in a flow.

question: Which function is used to add buttons, links, and context menu items to forms and lists?
explanation:
ServiceNow UI Actions define interactive controls on forms and lists, including form and list buttons, related links, and context-menu items.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: UI actions](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_UIActions.html?contentId=O5VhPOzlmtsfIWzc3NO23g)

question:
An Administrator needs to show a reminder message to every user who submits an incident.

Which feature accomplishes this?
explanation:
An onSubmit Client Script runs when a form is submitted and can display an alert or other custom form message to the user. ServiceNow documents that custom messages on forms can be added through client scripting.

**Learn more:** [Client scripts](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/yokohama/application-development/scripts/client-scripts.html) · [Scripting alert, info, and error messages](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/application-development/scripts/r_ScriptingAlertInfoAndErrorMsgs.html)

question: When importing data from a spreadsheet, which step specifies where the incoming data columns are written in the target table?
explanation:
Field matching maps each source spreadsheet column to its corresponding field in the target table, thereby determining where the imported values are stored.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Now Platform Utah release fact sheet](https://downloads.docs.servicenow.com/enus/utah/upgrade/utah-fact-sheet.pdf)

question: Which catalog tool would you use to create a catalog item or record producer?
explanation:
ServiceNow Catalog Builder provides a guided interface for creating or editing catalog items, including record producers.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Catalog Builder](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/catalog-builder.html)

question: You need to create a Service Catalog option that lets a user select **Get Help** and describe the issue they are experiencing. The form must create incident records that are automatically routed to the Service Desk. Which method should you use?
explanation:
A Record Producer provides a Service Catalog form that creates a task-based record directly, including an incident record, rather than creating a request and requested item. The resulting incident can use the platform's assignment or routing configuration to reach the Service Desk.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Record Producer](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_RecordProducer.html) · [ServiceNow: Create an incident](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/incident-management/create-an-incident.html)

question: What access is required for a user to import articles into a knowledge base?
explanation:
Importing an article creates a knowledge article in the target knowledge base. ServiceNow requires **Can Contribute** access to at least one active knowledge base to perform that action.

**Learn more:** [Import a Word document to a knowledge base](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/knowledge-management/import-word-platform.html)

question: What is a Dictionary Override?

options.label: A
options.text: A Dictionary Override is an incoming customer update in an Update Set which applies to the same objects as a newer local customer update

options.label: B
options.text: A Dictionary Override is the addition, modification, or removal of anything that could have an effect on IT services

options.label: C
options.text: A Dictionary Override is a task within a flow that requests an action before the flow can continue

options.label: D
options.text: A Dictionary Override sets field properties in extended tables

explanation:
A ServiceNow dictionary override changes field properties for an extended (child) table without changing the corresponding field definition on the parent table or other child tables. [ServiceNow: Dictionary overrides](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/c_DictionaryOverrides.html)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow — Dictionary overrides](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/c_DictionaryOverrides.html)

question: When you create a global custom table named `abc`, what table name does the platform automatically assign?
explanation: ServiceNow automatically prefixes custom tables created in the global scope with `u_`, so the resulting table name is `u_abc`.

question: If you want to manage your personal tasks using a visual drag-and-drop interface, which application would you use?
explanation: Visual Task Boards provide a visual, drag-and-drop board interface for creating, organizing, and managing tasks.

question: Which tool provides a graphical infrastructure view of a configuration item (CI) and its relationships with other CIs?
explanation: Dependency View graphically visualizes a configuration item and its relationships with other configuration items in the infrastructure.

question: A colleague wants to reorder the columns in their My Work List. After navigating to the list, where should the user go to choose and arrange the columns?

options.label: A
options.text: Right click on any column header, Context Menu > Configure > List Layout

options.label: B
options.text: Click List Context Menu > Configure > List Layout

options.label: C
options.text: Click List Context Menu > Personalize List

explanation:
Personal list layout changes apply only to the logged-in user and are made through **Personalize List**. By contrast, **Configure > List Layout** is used to configure a list layout for all users when the user has the appropriate role.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Best practices for configuring lists](https://www.servicenow.com/community/servicenow-ai-platform-blog/best-practices-for-configuring-lists/ba-p/2283363)

question: What is a Notification used for?

options.label: A
options.text: A new Knowledge article created by a Business Rule

options.label: B
options.text: A tool for alerting users that events that concern them have occurred

options.label: C
options.text: A message through Connect related to a Change Request

explanation:
A ServiceNow notification is a mechanism for alerting users about events or record changes that may concern them. It can be delivered through channels such as email, SMS, push notifications, or messaging apps.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow System notifications](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/system-notifications-landing.html)

question: Which of the following statements explains the purpose of a Service Catalog flow?

options.label: A
options.text: A Service Catalog flow generates three basic components: item variable types, tasks, and approvals

options.label: B
options.text: Although a Service Catalog flow cannot send notifications, the flow drives complex fulfillment processes

options.label: C
options.text: A Service Catalog flow is used to drive complex fulfillment processes and sends notifications to defined users or groups

options.label: D
options.text: A Service Catalog flow generates three basic components: item variable types, tasks, and notifications

explanation:
A Service Catalog flow automates a catalog item's fulfillment process. Workflow Studio flows can orchestrate multi-step fulfillment work and automate approvals, tasks, and notifications, including notifications directed to users or groups.

**Learn more:** [Service Catalog request fulfillment](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/request-fulfillment.html) · [Create a flow with a Service Catalog trigger](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/build-workflows/workflow-studio/create-sc-flow.html)

question: Which statement is true when a new table is created by extending an existing table?

options.label: A
options.text: The new table archives the parent table and assumed its roles in the database

options.label: B
options.text: The new table inherits all of the Business Rules, Client Scripts, and UI Policies of the parent table, but none of the existing fields

options.label: C
options.text: The new table inherits all of the fields of the parent table and can also contain new fields unique to itself

options.label: D
options.text: The new table inherits all of the fields, but does not inherit Access Control rules, Client Scripts, and UI Policies of the parent table

explanation:
In ServiceNow, a child table created by extending a parent table automatically inherits the parent’s fields and can add custom fields that are unique to the child table. Parent-table access controls also apply to tables that extend the parent.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Tables and data models](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/tables-and-data-models.html) · [ServiceNow: Create a table](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/t_CreateATable.html?contentId=8EfyhC9ilIfGGhbCb3bm0Q)

question: At what point does a Business Rule run in ServiceNow?

options.label: A
options.text: When a user downloads a report

options.label: B
options.text: Before or after a user logs into the platform

options.label: C
options.text: Before or after a record is saved to the database

options.label: D
options.text: Only when a record is deleted

explanation:
ServiceNow Business Rules can be configured to run synchronously before or after a database operation on a record. Before rules run as part of saving the record, while after rules run after the database operation completes.

**Learn more:** [Business rules and script includes](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/business-rules-and-script-includes.html)

question: Which option best describes a field in a ServiceNow table?

options.label: A
options.text: A field is a table row.

options.label: B
options.text: A field is an item that appears in a menu list.

options.label: C
options.text: A field is a table cell that stores data.

options.label: D
options.text: A field is a record in a table.

explanation: A ServiceNow field stores a specific data value within a record; it corresponds to a data-storing cell for that record.

question: Which section on the Notes tab displays the history of work documented on the record?
explanation:
The Activity section maintains the record’s activity stream, including work notes, comments, and updates, providing the documented history of work.

**Learn more:** [Using the activity stream in the contextual side panel](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/wLYnGFihvmNxBr5heMf_jw/sfX8yUDKx5_OGwivjiXJVg)

question: Which of the following statements describes an Order Guide’s purpose?

options.label: A
options.text: Order Guides restrict the number of items in an order to only one item per request

options.label: B
options.text: Order Guide provide a list of guidelines for Administrators on how to set up item variables

options.label: C
options.text: Order Guide provide the ability to order multiple, related items as one request

options.label: D
options.text: Order Guides take the user directly to the checkout without prompting for information

explanation: An Order Guide lets a requester order multiple related catalog items together as a single request, often using shared information to streamline fulfillment.

question: What is the primary application used for loading data into ServiceNow?
explanation: System Import Sets is the ServiceNow application used to import data from external sources, stage it in import-set tables, and transform it into target tables.

question:
A customer asks for these data-quality measures to be added:

- Incident numbers must be read-only on all lists and forms for every user.
- The **Short Description** field must be mandatory on all records, across all applications, when inserting.

Which type of policy would you use to satisfy this requirement?
explanation:
A ServiceNow data policy enforces field-level data consistency by defining mandatory and read-only states in data policy rules. It can enforce these requirements beyond a particular form or application context, including data submitted through supported non-browser channels.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Data policy](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_DataPolicy.html?contentId=bkk032GHpRWxBckoW_~lZA) · [ServiceNow Data policy fields](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/r_DataPolicyFields.html?contentId=I3oJOsCNRk0lW_4vQQpquw)

question: Which action can be chosen to apply predefined or custom conditions that filter and generate specified data in the Visualization Designer?
explanation: In ServiceNow Visualization Designer, **Preview** applies the configured conditions and displays the resulting filtered data so the visualization can be evaluated before it is saved or used.

question: What should you click after making changes to your report when you want to view the results without saving?
explanation:
In ServiceNow Report Designer, **Run** generates the report from the conditions and layout currently selected; saving the report is a separate action.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Create a report — Report options](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/reporting/t_CreateYourOwnReport.html)

question: Which icon is used to change the label of a Favorite?
explanation: A pencil icon conventionally indicates an edit action, including changing an item's label.

question: When working with a form, what distinguishes Insert operations from Update operations?

options.label: A
options.text: Insert creates a new record and Update saves changes, both remain on the form

options.label: B
options.text: Insert creates a new record and Update saves changes, both exit the form

options.label: C
options.text: Insert saves changes and exits the form, Update saves changes and remains on the form

options.label: D
options.text: Insert saves changes and remains on the form, Update saves changes and exits the form

explanation:
In ServiceNow, **Insert** saves the item as a new record, while **Update** saves changes to an existing record. Both standard actions return to the previously viewed page; staying on the form requires a separate action such as **Insert and Stay** or **Save**.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Edit a form](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/t_EditingInForms.html)

question: IntegrationHub allows third-party APIs to be executed as part of a flow. These integrations are called
explanation:
IntegrationHub lets a flow call third-party APIs, and these pre-built integrations are packaged and called spokes (B). A spoke is a scoped application bundling related Flow Designer actions and sub-flows for a specific external system (for example Slack, Microsoft Teams, or Ansible). An 'action' (A) is a single building block within a spoke or flow, not the name for the integration package, and a 'connection' is the credential/endpoint definition, so B is the precise term.

**Learn more:** [IntegrationHub spokes list](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/integrate-applications/integration-hub/spokes-list.html) · [What is IntegrationHub and how do I use it?](https://www.servicenow.com/community/developer-blog/what-is-integrationhub-and-how-do-i-use-it/ba-p/2289972)

question: What does an Access Control rule specify?

options.label: B
options.text: Table Schema, CRUD, and User Authentication

options.label: C
options.text: Object and Operation being secured; Permissions required to access the object

explanation:
A ServiceNow Access Control List (ACL) rule identifies the object to secure and the operation being controlled, and it defines the conditions or permissions required for access. [Explore Access Control Lists](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/access-control/exploring-access-control-list.html)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Explore Access Control Lists](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/access-control/exploring-access-control-list.html)

question: Which section of a task record lets you view the most recent updates to the record?
explanation:
The Activity Stream displays a running history of record activity, including field changes, comments, work notes, and emails, with the latest updates available in the stream.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Activity streams](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/c_activity-streams.html)

question: Which field type provides a drop-down list from which you can select predefined options?
explanation: A Choice field stores a selection from a predefined list of options and is commonly displayed as a drop-down control.

question: Which feature can monitor how long a task has remained open, helping ensure that tasks are completed within an allotted timeframe?
explanation: Service level agreements define time-based targets for tasks and track their elapsed and remaining time so work can be completed within the required timeframe.

question: When you add a related list to a form, you select it from the list collector. Which of the following is an example of a related list that could appear in the list collector? (select 3)
explanation:
ServiceNow automatically provides related lists for records connected through reference fields. In the list collector, these relationships are identified as the related table followed by the reference field, using `->`, such as `HR Case->Parent`, `Catalog Task->Parent`, and `Outage->Task number`.

**Learn more:** [Tables and data models](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/tables-and-data-models.html) · [Add a related list](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/employee-service-management/universal-task/create-relatedlist-ur.html?contentId=gKAasQ8U8SholL5BpINw8Q)

question: A REQ number in the Service Catalog denotes:

options.label: D
options.text: the individual item in the order.

explanation:
A Service Catalog order creates a request record, identified by a REQ number, to track the overall order. Individual catalog items receive separate requested-item (RITM) records, while fulfillment work is handled through tasks.

**Learn more:** [Service Catalog request screens](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_RequestingAServiceCatalogItem.html)

question: Which three security modules are commonly used by the System Administrator? *(select 3)*
explanation:
System administrators use the Security module under System Properties to configure security-related instance settings, Access Control (ACL) to define authorization rules for platform objects and data, and Security Questions under Password Management to administer password-recovery questions. ServiceNow documents ACL administration under **System Security > Access Control (ACL)**.

**Learn more:** [Configure an ACL rule](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/access-control/t_CreateAnACLRule.html)

question: Which feature do you use to define which users can access a Service Catalog item?
explanation:
ServiceNow User Criteria determines which users can access a Service Catalog item. Criteria records can be applied to items through Available For and Not Available For settings, and they evaluate user attributes to allow or restrict access.

**Learn more:** [Apply user criteria to items and categories](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/t_AppUserCritItemsCat.html)

question: As an IT employee, which interface would you use to browse internal IT documentation, such as troubleshooting scripts and FAQs?
explanation:
ServiceNow Knowledge Management provides knowledge bases containing internal articles for self-help, troubleshooting, and task resolution, and users can browse or search those articles. ამიტომ the appropriate interface is Knowledge.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Knowledge Management](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/knowledge-management/knowledge-management.html)

question: Which core ServiceNow platform table supplies a set of standard fields for every table that extends it, including the Incident [incident] and Problem [problem] tables?
explanation:
The Task [task] table is the parent table for Incident [incident] and Problem [problem]. Tables that extend Task inherit its shared standard fields and task-related functionality.

**Learn more:** [Working with the Task table](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/zurich/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/c_TaskTable.html)

question: Which form element shows the activity list, or history, on a task form?
explanation: The Activity Formatter displays a task record’s activity stream and history on the form, including updates and journal entries.

question: Which tool defines relationships between fields in an import set table and a target table?
explanation:
A Transform Map specifies how an import set table maps to a target table and contains the field maps that associate source fields with destination fields during the transformation.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Transform maps](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/integrate-applications/system-import-sets/c_CreatingNewTransformMaps.html)

question: Which field on each record holds that record's unique identifier?
explanation:
The `sys_id` field is the unique 32-character GUID that identifies each ServiceNow record.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Unique record identifier (sys_id)](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_UniqueRecordIdentifier.html)

question: Access Control rules apply to a particular table, such as the Incident table. What is the object name for a rule specific to the Incident table and the Major Incident field?
explanation:
A ServiceNow field-level record ACL is named with the table name followed by a period and the field’s internal name. ServiceNow documents this syntax with examples such as `incident.number`; therefore, the Major Incident field on the Incident table is identified as `incident.major_incident`.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow ACL types](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/access-control/acl-rule-types.html)

question: When a policy is configured to apply to all data entering the platform—whether through the UI, Import Sets, or Web Services—where does that policy execute by default?
explanation:
Data Policies in ServiceNow are designed to enforce field-level rules (such as mandatory or read-only) across every method of data entry, including imports and web service calls that never pass through a browser. To guarantee this consistent enforcement, Data Policies execute on the server by default, rather than relying on client-side (browser) scripting like UI Policies do. An optional 'Enforce on client' checkbox can be enabled to also apply the equivalent behavior in the browser, but the default and guaranteed execution point is the server.

**Learn more:** [Data policies - ServiceNow Product Documentation](https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/utah-platform-administration/page/administer/table-administration/concept/c_DataPolicies.html)

question: Which of the following best describes the primary operations carried out on tables in the ServiceNow platform?
explanation:
ServiceNow table records support CRUD operations: create, read, update, and delete. “Write” is the corresponding choice term for modifying an existing record, making Create, Read, Write, Delete the intended CRUD set.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Table API](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/rest-apis/c_TableAPI.html)

question: Which access control rules are automatically generated when a custom table is created? (select 4)
explanation:
The automatically configured table access controls cover the four CRUD operations: create, read, write, and delete. In ServiceNow ACL terminology, the **write** operation authorizes updating records; **update** is not a separate record ACL operation. **Execute** applies to executable resources such as client-callable Script Includes and REST endpoint execution, not standard table CRUD access.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Secure data](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/secure-data.html) · [ServiceNow: ACL types](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/access-control/acl-rule-types.html)

question:
Consider this example criteria set for a knowledge base:

- Companies: ACME North America
- Departments: HR
- Groups: ACME Managers
- Match All: Yes

In this example, which users would be able to access this knowledge base?

options.label: A
options.text: Members of the ACME Manager group, who are also members of HR Department and part of ACME North America

options.label: B
options.text: Employees of ACME North America, who are members of HR Department or the ACME Managers group

options.label: C
options.text: Users which are members of either ACME North America, or HR Department, or ACME Managers group

options.label: D
options.text: Members of the ACME Managers group, and HR department, regardless of geography

explanation:
With **Match All** selected, ServiceNow grants access only to users who satisfy every populated user-criteria field. Access therefore requires membership in ACME North America, the HR department, and the ACME Managers group.

**Learn more:** [Create user criteria for controlling access to knowledge bases and articles](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/knowledge-management/create-user-criteria-record-in-knowledge-management.html?contentId=bT01Br4X1ELNA87JotWPtg)

question: Which of the following statements describes what the Configuration Management Database (CMDB) contains?

options.label: A
options.text: The CMDB contains data about tangible and intangible business assets

options.label: B
options.text: The CMDB contains the Business Rules that direct the intangible, configurable assets used by a company

options.label: C
options.text: The CMDB archives all Service Management PaaS equipment metadata and usage statistics

options.label: D
options.text: The CMDB contains ITIL process data pertaining to configuration items

explanation:
A CMDB stores information about configuration items that represent an organization’s tangible and intangible assets, including physical infrastructure, software, services, and their relationships. ServiceNow describes the CMDB as storing logical representations of assets, services, and their relationships as configuration items.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Configuration Management Database (CMDB)](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/c_ITILConfigurationManagement.html)

question: Which tool is used to populate commonly used fields on a form?
explanation:
A ServiceNow form template saves predefined field values and populates them when the template is applied, making it suitable for commonly used form fields. [ServiceNow: Form templates](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_Templates.html)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Form templates](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_Templates.html)

question: Which information is contained in the System Dictionary?

options.label: A
options.text: The human-readable labels and language settings

options.label: B
options.text: The definition for each table and column

options.label: C
options.text: The information on how tables relate to each other

options.label: D
options.text: The language dictionary used for spell checking

explanation:
The System Dictionary (`sys_dictionary`) defines every table and field (column) in a ServiceNow instance and stores their attributes, such as data type, character limit, and default value.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Data dictionary tables](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/c_DataDictionaryTables.html)

question: Which Service Catalog feature is used to organize items into logical groups?
explanation: Service Catalog categories organize catalog items into logical groups, making offerings easier for users to browse and locate.

question: What distinguishes a UI Policy from a Data Policy?

options.label: A
options.text: Data Policies run when data is entered through the form, by an Import Set, or by web services, while UI Policies are set only by web services

options.label: B
options.text: Data Policies can be converted into UI Policies, but UI Policies cannot be converted into Data Policies

options.label: C
options.text: Data Policies run regardless of how data is entered into ServiceNow, while UI Policies are used for form interactions

options.label: D
options.text: Data Policies run only after UI Policies run successfully

explanation:
Data Policies enforce mandatory and read-only field rules for data entering ServiceNow through multiple channels, including forms, import sets, and web services. UI Policies control client-side form interactions and behavior, including field visibility. [ServiceNow Data policy](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_DataPolicy.html?contentId=bkk032GHpRWxBckoW_~lZA)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Data policy](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_DataPolicy.html?contentId=bkk032GHpRWxBckoW_~lZA) · [ServiceNow Using UI policies](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/t_CreateAUIPolicy.html)

question: When impersonating a user for testing, what is the best method for returning to the instance while logged in with your own user account?

options.label: A
options.text: Turn your computer off and on again

explanation:
ServiceNow’s **End Impersonation** action ends the current impersonation session and restores the original user login. [ServiceNow: Impersonate a user](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/user-administration/t_ImpersonateAUserInUI16.html)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow — Impersonate a user](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/user-administration/t_ImpersonateAUserInUI16.html)

question: Which icon is used to change a Favorite’s label?
explanation:
Salesforce Lightning Experience uses the pencil icon for editing and renaming items in Favorites.

**Learn more:** [Navigate Lightning Experience Effectively](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/it/content/learn/modules/lightning-experience-for-salesforce-classic-users/navigate-around)

question: Which of the following items are not included in an Update Set by default? (select 4)
explanation:
Update Sets capture customization and configuration changes but not operational data. By default they do NOT include Data records (B), Homepages/content pages (A), Schedules and scheduled jobs (E), and published Workflows (C) unless manually added or specifically promoted. In contrast, Business Rules (D) are standard configuration records tracked automatically, and Database/schema changes (F) made through the Dictionary are also captured by default, which is why the blind answer's inclusion of F is wrong. That leaves exactly the four operational/content items ABCE as not captured.

**Learn more:** [What is not captured in Update Sets?](https://www.servicenow.com/community/developer-forum/what-is-not-captured-in-update-sets/td-p/2844441) · [Mastering ServiceNow Update Sets](https://www.georgehenryschneider.com/?p=22)

question:
Two departments—HR Onboarding and Facilities—have asked you for a way for employees to request event room setup services. The requirements for the form and task routing to the Facilities assignment group are identical.

- For HR, the item will be used mainly by Onboarding coordinators for employee orientation sessions.
- For Facilities, the item will be used by anyone in the company who requires room setup services.

However, both departments maintain their own service catalogs. What should you do to support these requirements?

options.label: A
options.text: Create one Catalog Item for HR Event Room Set Up and one for Facilities Event Room Set Up; then publish each to the appropriate Catalog.

options.label: B
options.text: Create one Catalog Item for Event Room Set Up; then publish to both Catalogs.

options.label: C
options.text: Create one Catalog Item for Event Room Set Up; then publish to the Parent Catalog, which is accessible to both HR and Facilities.

options.label: D
options.text: Create one Catalog Item for Event Room Set Up; then use ACLs to control access.

explanation:
ServiceNow allows one catalog item to be shared across multiple catalogs. Publishing the same Event Room Set Up item in both the HR and Facilities catalogs preserves one common form and one fulfillment process that routes tasks to the Facilities assignment group, without duplicating the item.

**Learn more:** [Share catalog items across catalogs](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/t_ShareCatalogItemsAcrossCatalogs.html)

question: A new service catalog item is being developed, but it should be visible only to managers within the HR Department. Which method would you use to meet this requirement?

options.label: A
options.text: Specify the Dept_Mgr role on the catalog content block

options.label: B
options.text: Add the Department Manager group to the catalog item's user criteria

options.label: C
options.text: Add the Department Manager group to the catalog item's ACL

options.label: D
options.text: Only publish the item in the HR service catalog

options.label: E
options.text: Use a Dept_Mgr ACL on the HR service catalog

explanation:
ServiceNow User Criteria controls access to individual Service Catalog items. A criterion based on membership in the Department Manager group can be assigned to the catalog item’s **Available For** list, restricting its visibility to those managers.

**Learn more:** [Apply user criteria to items and categories](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/t_AppUserCritItemsCat.html) · [Create a user criteria record in Service Catalog](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/t_CreateAUserCriteriaRecord.html)

question: Which feature lets business process owners organize Flow Designer content into unified, digitized cross-enterprise processes through a digitized task-board interface?
explanation:
ServiceNow Process Automation Designer enables business process owners to combine Flow Designer flows and actions into unified cross-enterprise processes. Its Playbooks design environment organizes activities through a digitized task-board or diagram interface.

**Learn more:** [Exploring Playbooks](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/build-workflows/workflow-studio/process-automation-designer.html)

question: Which statement below explains how data is structured in a table?

options.label: A
options.text: A column is a field in the database and a record is one user

options.label: B
options.text: A column is one field and a record is one row

options.label: C
options.text: A column is one field and a record is one column

options.label: D
options.text: A column contains data from one user and a record is one set of fields

explanation: A table organizes attributes as columns (fields) and individual entries as records (rows).

question: Which of the following controls the display sequence in a Service Catalog Item?

options.label: A
options.text: The Default Value field in the Catalog Item form

options.label: B
options.text: The Sequence field in the Catalog Item form

options.label: C
options.text: The Order field in the Variable form

options.label: D
options.text: The Choice field in the Variable form

explanation: A Service Catalog variable’s **Order** field determines its position in the catalog item’s displayed variable sequence.

question: Access Control rules apply to a specific table, such as the Incident table. What is the object name for a rule that applies to the entire Incident table, including all rows and fields?
explanation: A record-level ServiceNow ACL for an entire table uses the naming format `<table>.None`. For the Incident table, that object name is `incident.None`.

question: By default, which knowledge workers can create and edit categories in the knowledge base? (select 2)
explanation:
Knowledge contributors can add and edit categories through the Category picker when editing knowledge articles, unless category editing has been disabled for the knowledge base. Knowledge managers are responsible for defining the category structure of a knowledge base.

**Learn more:** [Select a knowledge article category](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/knowledge-management/t_SelectACategory.html?contentId=fPElqKp621lQ7W1OjHn3uw) · [Configuration tasks for knowledge managers](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/knowledge-management/c_KnowledgeManager.html)

question: Which path can an Administrator use to view the fulfillment-stage task list for an order submitted by a user?
explanation:
A Service Catalog order produces a request (REQ), with each ordered catalog item represented by a requested item (RITM). Fulfillment tasks are associated with the requested item and are available through its Catalog Tasks related list.

**Learn more:** [Service Catalog request screens](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_RequestingAServiceCatalogItem.html) · [Define an item task](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/washingtondc/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/t_DefineAnItemTask.html)

question: Which database provides a logical model of your company infrastructure by identifying, controlling, maintaining, and verifying the CIs that exist?
explanation: A CMDB records configuration items and their relationships, creating a logical model of an organization’s infrastructure for configuration management.

question: In Flow Designer, where is an action’s data stored so that it can be used by later actions in the flow?
explanation:
Each action added to a flow has an action-result data pill that stores its results. Those data pills can be used as inputs by subsequent actions in the flow.

**Learn more:** [Data pills](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/fr-FR/build-workflows/workflow-studio/data-population.html) · [Input and output data variables](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/build-workflows/workflow-studio/action-inputs-outputs.html)

question: Which best practice does ServiceNow recommend for data imports?

options.label: A
options.text: Adjust your Transform maps, after the data is loaded into the target table.

options.label: B
options.text: Use extremely large Import Sets, instead of multiple large Import Sets.

options.label: C
options.text: Create a new Import set table for each new data load.

options.label: D
options.text: Plan time before your import to remove obsolete or inaccurate data.

options.label: E
options.text: Monitor data quality and clean imported data, using the Data Scrub Workspace.

explanation: Source data should be reviewed and cleansed before an import so obsolete or inaccurate records are not introduced into the ServiceNow instance. This prevents avoidable data-quality issues in target tables.

question: When using the Load Data and Transform Map process, what is Mapping Assist used for?

options.label: A
options.text: Mapping fields using the Import Log

options.label: D
options.text: Mapping fields using a Field Map

explanation:
Mapping Assist manually pairs fields from the staging table with fields in the target table, creating the transform map’s Field Map mappings. Import Log and Transform History record import activity, while an SLA is unrelated to field mapping.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Developer: Mapping Assist](https://developer.servicenow.com/print_page.do?category=learning-module&identifier=app_store_learnv2_importingdata_xanadu_importing_data_objectives%2Cnew_to_servicenow&module=learning+plan&release=xanadu)

question: An administrator creates the `customer_table_admin` and `customer_table_user` roles for the newly created **Customer Table**. Which ACL rule grants both the `customer_table_admin` and `customer_table_user` roles access to all rows and all fields?
explanation:
A `customer.none` record ACL is the table-level ACL for the Customer table. Passing a table ACL grants access to the table’s records, and ServiceNow evaluates table-level access before field-level access. A `customer.*` rule applies to all fields but does not replace the required table-level ACL.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow ACL types](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/access-control/acl-rule-types.html) · [ServiceNow Explore Access Control Lists](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/access-control/exploring-access-control-list.html)

question: When creating an extended table from a base table, which fields must you create? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: The fields that are not in the base table.

options.label: B
options.text: The mandatory fields for the base table.

options.label: C
options.text: The fields that are specific to the extended table.

options.label: D
options.text: The reference fields for the base table.

explanation:
Child tables inherit the fields and functionality of their parent/base tables automatically, while adding their own custom fields. Therefore, fields not present on the base table and fields specific to the extended table must be created.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Tables and data models](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/tables-and-data-models.html)

question: Which icon is used to change a Favorite’s icon and color?
explanation:
ServiceNow uses the pencil-shaped Edit Favorites control to enter the mode where a Favorite’s icon and color can be changed. The star is used to add favorites, and the clock represents navigation history.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Managing your favorites](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/zurich/platform-user-interface/configure-user-experiences/managing-your-favorites.html)

question: What is the platform table name for the User table?
explanation: ServiceNow stores user records in the standard `sys_user` table.

question: Which applications enable administrators to create and distribute data visualizations? (select 2)
explanation:
ServiceNow Reporting creates shareable visual reports of current instance data. Performance Analytics creates visual representations of KPI and indicator data through widgets, which can be presented on dashboards for sharing.

**Learn more:** [Reporting](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/reporting/reporting-landing-page.html) · [Performance Analytics widgets](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/performance-analytics/c_Widgets.html)

question:
Which collaboration tool can be accessed from the banner by using the bubble icon?

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783808870199-nu2xo8jx.png)
explanation:
In the ServiceNow Core UI, the Connect sidebar icon in the banner lets users begin or continue conversations. Connect Chat is the real-time collaboration tool for individual and group chats and record-based collaboration.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Core UI](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/washingtondc/platform-user-interface/c_UI16.html) · [ServiceNow Connect Chat](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/connect/c_Collaboration.html)

question: Which types of entities can be assigned tasks in ServiceNow? (select 2)
explanation:
ServiceNow task assignment supports assigning work to an individual user through the **Assigned to** field and to a user group through the **Assignment group** field. Assignment rules can automatically assign a task to either a user or a group.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Assignment rules](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/c_DefineAssignmentRules.html?contentId=sfF5b41gdpeqe3Ijy0orBg)

question: What is the name of the string that displays the filter criteria?
explanation:
In ServiceNow, breadcrumbs are the hierarchical list of conditions at the top of a table that indicates the current filter.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Filters and breadcrumbs](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/c_UsingFiltersAndBreadcrumbs.html)

question: Which storefront provides a single place to access pre-built spokes, enabling quick integration with third-party services to build and share content?
explanation:
The ServiceNow Store is the single storefront that provides pre-built IntegrationHub spokes — application-specific sets of actions and subflows — enabling quick integration with third-party services such as Salesforce, Slack, and Teams, and where partners and customers build and share content. There is no product called "Integration Spoke Store," "Spoke Store," or "ServiceNow Spoke Store"; those are distractors, so option A is correct.

**Learn more:** [Integration Hub](https://www.servicenow.com/products/integration-hub.html) · [ServiceNow Store](https://store.servicenow.com/)

question: Which metric in Security Center indicates the level of instance hardening?
explanation:
The Compliance score measures how closely an instance’s security settings conform to the recommended hardening settings, so it represents the instance’s hardening level.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Security hardening](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/security-center/sc-hardening.html) · [ServiceNow Security configuration console](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/security-center/homepage.html)

question: Which actions would you use to edit an application menu’s title? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Select the Application name on the Navigator, then select the pencil icon

options.label: C
options.text: Select System Definitions > Application Menus then select the application

options.label: D
options.text: Select Configuration > Applications, then select the application

options.label: E
options.text: Select the form for the Application, then right-click, Configure > Form Designer

explanation:
An application’s navigator title is stored on its Application Menu record. That record can be opened from the Navigator’s edit control for the application or from **System Definition > Application Menus**, where its name can be changed.

**Learn more:** [Securing Applications and Modules](https://developer.servicenow.com/print_page.do?category=courses&identifier=app_store_learnv2_securingapps_zurich_securing_applications&module=course&release=zurich)

question: Which Security Center feature helps address platform-related security issues and misconfigurations?
explanation:
The Security Center's Security hardening feature is what specifically addresses platform-related security issues and misconfigurations: it measures how closely an instance's configuration conforms to ServiceNow's recommended secure baseline, surfaces non-compliant settings and a hardening compliance score, and lets administrators remediate the drift. "Best practices" and "Customer actions" are supporting areas of Security Center but are not the feature that pinpoints platform misconfigurations, and the Security scanner focuses on running check suites (often access-control checks) rather than baseline hardening, so option C is correct.

**Learn more:** [Security hardening](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/security-center/sc-hardening.html) · [Security Center](https://store.servicenow.com/store/app/cc1befe61b246a50a85b16db234bcbf1)

question: Which module lets an administrator define destinations for imported data on any ServiceNow table?
explanation:
A transform map defines how fields in an import set are mapped to destination fields in an existing ServiceNow table. The Transform Maps module is used to define those destinations for imported data. [ServiceNow: Transform maps](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/integrate-applications/system-import-sets/c_CreatingNewTransformMaps.html)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow documentation: Transform maps](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/integrate-applications/system-import-sets/c_CreatingNewTransformMaps.html)

question: What is the main purpose of Form Builder on the Now Platform?

options.label: A
options.text: To create new tables within the platform

options.label: B
options.text: To generate analytical reports from data tables

options.label: C
options.text: To configure system settings and permissions

options.label: D
options.text: To edit forms used for populating records

explanation:
Form Builder customizes and edits the forms used to enter and populate records, including their fields and layout.

**Learn more:** [Accessing Form Builder](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/form-builder-glide-family-release/access-form-builder.html)

question: You need to create a way for users to order a new iPhone, but only after receiving two levels of approval. Approvers and users must be notified automatically at each approval level. Which feature would you use to manage the approvals and notifications?
explanation:
Approval Chains define the specific approvers and their sequence for a serial approval workflow. They support multi-level approvals in which each approver completes the assigned task before the next approver receives it, with approval notifications sent to the appropriate recipients.

**Learn more:** [Approval Workflow Types](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ind.approvals_types_of_approvals.htm&language=en_US&type=5) · [Approval Rule Fields](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.cpq_approval_rule_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5)

question: What is meant by a Record Producer?

options.label: A
options.text: A Record Producer is a type of Catalog Item that is used for Requests, not Services

options.label: B
options.text: A Record Producer creates user records

options.label: C
options.text: A Record Producer is a type of Catalog Item that provides easy ordering by bundling requests

options.label: D
options.text: A Record Producer is a type of a Catalog Item that allows users to create task-based records from the Service Catalog

explanation:
A Record Producer is a specific type of ServiceNow catalog item that enables end users to create task-based records, such as incident records, through the Service Catalog rather than creating a requested item. [ServiceNow Record Producer documentation](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_RecordProducer.html)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow — Record Producer](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_RecordProducer.html)

question: A new Service Desk employee in Latin America reports that the create dates and times on their Incident list are incorrect. What would you recommend to resolve this issue?

options.label: B
options.text: Have them use the gear icon to set the employee's time zone.

options.label: C
options.text: Recommend they use Chrome, instead of Explorer.

options.label: D
options.text: Use the system properties to correct the instance's time zone.

options.label: E
options.text: Have them correct the time zone on their computer.

explanation:
ServiceNow stores time values in UTC and renders them according to each user’s time-zone preferences.
