Users can change the time zone for their current session through System Settings, accessed with the gear icon; changing the instance time zone would affect other users and is not appropriate for an individual display issue.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Time zones](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/time-configuration/r_TimeZones.html)

question: What is the definition of a group?

options.label: A
options.text: A collection of subject matter experts

explanation: A group is a collection of users, commonly used to manage access, permissions, or policies for multiple users together.

question: On a form header, what is the name of the three-bar icon?
explanation: The conventional name for an icon made of three horizontal bars is the hamburger icon.

question: Which ServiceNow capability helps users obtain information, make decisions, and complete common work tasks through a messaging interface?
explanation:
ServiceNow Virtual Agent provides automated conversational assistance through an intelligent messaging interface, enabling users to obtain information, make decisions, and perform common work tasks.

**Learn more:** [Exploring Virtual Agent](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/conversational-interfaces/virtual-agent/exploring-virtual-agent.html?contentId=5ABaifUBvfYGiBsXDBu6wA)

question: Which features let you update multiple records simultaneously? (select 2)
explanation:
ServiceNow’s List Editor supports editing fields for multiple records in a list, while **Update Selected** applies an update to every selected record. ServiceNow documentation states that selecting **Update Selected** updates all selected records.

**Learn more:** [Configure and use list functions](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/configure-use-list-functions.html)

question: After completing your work on High Security Settings, what is a possible way to return to normal administrator security levels?

options.label: E
options.text: Use System Administration > Normal Security module

explanation: Logging out ends the session in which the security_admin role was temporarily elevated. Logging back in begins a new session with normal administrator security levels.

question: On the Reports page, which sections let you see reports that are visible to different audiences? (select 4)
explanation:
The Reports page organizes reports by their sharing audience into sections: My reports (C, reports you created), Group (A, reports shared with specific groups), Global (F, reports shared with everyone), and All. Of these, only My reports, Group, and Global appear among the offered choices, so ACF is correct. Department (B), Team (D), and Dashboards (E) are not report-visibility sections, which is why the blind answer's inclusion of Team is wrong; the fourth genuine section ('All') is simply not among the options here.

**Learn more:** [Making my reports visible to all](https://www.servicenow.com/community/developer-forum/making-my-reports-visible-to-all/m-p/2227752) · [ServiceNow Reporting](https://support.rowan.edu/kb_view.do?sys_kb_id=384408fddba15344873cf6e9af961967&sysparm_media=print)

question: Which actions can you use to open the Context Menu on a list, form, or column? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Select the Context Menu related link

options.label: B
options.text: Double-click on the list form or column heading

options.label: C
options.text: Right-click on the list, form or column heading

explanation:
ServiceNow provides context menus through a right-click on the relevant list, form header, or column heading, and through the Context Menu icon. The form context-menu documentation specifically identifies clicking the icon beside the form title or right-clicking the form header as supported access methods.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Form context menu](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/c_FormContextMenu.html)

question: In which table are group records stored?
explanation: ServiceNow stores group records in the out-of-box Group table, whose database table name is `sys_user_group`.

question: When transferring multiple update sets at the same time, what can you do to facilitate the transfer?
explanation:
Batch update sets group multiple completed update sets so they can be previewed and committed together as a single batch, helping preserve the appropriate processing order and avoid omitting a set.

**Learn more:** [Working with batched update sets](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/system-update-sets/us-hier-overview.html)

question: Which of the following is **NOT** a type of Visual Task Board?
explanation:
ServiceNow Visual Task Boards are available as freeform, flexible, and guided boards. “Feature” is not a Visual Task Board type.

**Learn more:** [Using Visual Task Boards](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/visual-task-boards/working-in-vtb.html)

question: When an administrator configures a policy that applies to all data entered into the Platform (UI, Import Sets, or Web Services), where does that policy run by default?
explanation:
ServiceNow data policies enforce data consistency for records entered through the UI, import sets, and web services. They run server-side by default; client-side behavior is an optional UI-policy setting.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Data policy documentation](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_DataPolicy.html?contentId=bkk032GHpRWxBckoW_~lZA)

question: Which type of query lets you filter list data with ordinary words rather than using the condition builder?
explanation:
Natural Language Query (NLQ) accepts requests in everyday language and translates them into structured list-query conditions, removing the need to construct filters manually in the condition builder.

**Learn more:** [Using Natural Language Query](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/intelligent-experiences/natural-language-query/using-nlq.html)

question: On the Reports page, which sections let you see reports that are visible to different audiences? (select 4)
explanation:
ServiceNow organizes the Reports list into **My reports** for reports the user created, **Group** for reports shared with the user’s groups, **Global** for reports available to everyone, and **All** for every report the user is authorized to access.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: View the Reports list](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/reporting/r_ViewTheReportsList.html?contentId=yuLb6jp04r2~pz~Gbn9gdg)

question: Which item would **not** be shown in the Application Navigator when `service` is entered in the filter field?
explanation:
The Application Navigator filter shows matching application menus and modules. “Configuration > Business Services,” “Self-Service > Knowledge,” and “Service Portal > Widgets” match `service` in a menu or module name, whereas “Incident > Assigned to me” does not. [ServiceNow: Core UI application navigator](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/c_UI16ApplicationNavigator.html?contentId=4mUVNJsnD7ruzqY76LpBRQ)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Core UI application navigator](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/c_UI16ApplicationNavigator.html?contentId=4mUVNJsnD7ruzqY76LpBRQ)

question: Which of the following statements is a ServiceNow recommendation regarding Update Sets?

options.label: A
options.text: Avoid using the Default Update set as an Update Set for moving customizations from instance to instance

options.label: B
options.text: Before moving customizations from instance to instance with Update Sets, ensure that both instances are different versions

options.label: C
options.text: Use the Baseline Update Set to store the contents of items after they are changed the first time

options.label: D
options.text: Once an Update Set is closed as ג€Completeג€, change it back to ג€In Progressג€ until it is applied to another instance

explanation:
Avoid using the Default Update Set to move customizations between instances. ServiceNow states that the global default update set provides system functionality and should not be changed, deleted, or moved between systems.

**Learn more:** [Default update set](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/system-update-sets/default-update-sets.html) · [General guidelines for planning the update process](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/system-update-sets/get-started-update-sets.html)

question: In which part of the ServiceNow instance can you find the **Impersonate User** option?
explanation: The **Impersonate User** command is located in the ServiceNow user menu, which contains session and profile-related actions for the currently signed-in user.

question: Which framework can automatically fill the **Priority** and **Category** field values according to the value in the **Short description** field?
explanation: Predictive Intelligence classification models learn from historical records and use text inputs such as a short description to predict and populate target fields, including Category and Priority.

question: Which process enables users to create, categorize, review, approve, and browse important information in a centralized location shared across the entire organization?
explanation:
Knowledge Management governs the lifecycle of organizational knowledge articles: users can create and categorize content, route it for review and approval, and search or browse the published information in shared knowledge bases.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Exploring Knowledge Management](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/knowledge-management/exploring-knowledge-management.html)

question: If a knowledge base has no access details configured, which users can read articles in that knowledge base?

options.label: B
options.text: Any user with an article's permalink

explanation:
With no knowledge-base access criteria specified, read access defaults to all active users. Reading knowledge articles does not require the `itil` or `kb_user` role; roles and criteria are used when access is explicitly restricted.

**Learn more:** [Managing access to knowledge bases and knowledge articles](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/knowledge-management/user-access-knowledge.html)

question: What is the proper order for specifying filter elements?
explanation: A filter condition identifies the field being evaluated, applies a comparison operator to that field, and supplies the value against which the field is compared.

question: Which three variable types may be added to a Service Catalog item?

options.label: C
options.text: Number List, Single Line Text, and Reference

options.label: D
options.text: Multiple Choice, Select Box, and Checkbox

explanation:
Multiple Choice, Select Box, and CheckBox are supported Service Catalog variable types. ServiceNow’s variable-support documentation lists all three types.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Variable support in various channels](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/variables-availability.html)

question: Which statement is accurate about business rules?

options.label: A
options.text: A business rule must run before a database action occurs

options.label: B
options.text: A business rule can be a piece of Javascript

options.label: C
options.text: A business rule must not run before a database action occurs

options.label: D
options.text: A business rule monitors fields on a form

explanation:
A ServiceNow business rule is a server-side script and can contain JavaScript. Its execution timing is configurable (for example, before, after, async, or display), rather than being required to occur only before or only after a database action. [ServiceNow Classic business rules](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/business-rules-classic/c_BusinessRules.html)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Classic business rules](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/business-rules-classic/c_BusinessRules.html)

question:
The customer has requested a change to the default layout of the Task list. They want the following columns, in this order:

- Number
- Task Type
- Parent
- Short Description
- Assignment Group
- Assignee
- Updated

After navigating to the list, where would you click to fulfill this requirement?

options.label: A
options.text: Click List Context Menu > Personalize List

options.label: B
options.text: Click List Context Menu > Configure > Columns

options.label: C
options.text: Right click List Gear icon > Configure > Columns

options.label: D
options.text: Right click on any column header, Context Menu > Configure > List Layout

explanation:
ServiceNow list layout configuration controls the columns displayed in a list and their order for the selected view. It is accessed by right-clicking any column heading and choosing **Configure > List Layout**; list personalization is user-specific rather than a change to the default layout.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Configure the list layout](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/de-DE/platform-administration/list-administration/t_ConfigureTheListLayout.html?contentId=ZbfHdz_dPU6vn3KItauGqw)

question: Which interface enables users to search articles, submit requests, and browse communication notices?
explanation:
Service Portal is ServiceNow’s branded self-service site for requesters. Its Knowledge Management widgets support searching and reading articles, Service Catalog widgets support submitting requests, and portal configuration supports announcements. [ServiceNow: Widget library](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/service-portal/widget-showcase.html)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Widget library](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/service-portal/widget-showcase.html) · [ServiceNow Service Portal vs Workspace](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/dev-get-start-service-portal-vs-workspace.html)

question: While viewing an Incident record, how would you add the **Special Handling** tag to that record?

options.label: A
options.text: Click on the Context menu, select Add Tag, type Special Handling, press enter

options.label: B
options.text: Click on the More options (...) icon, click Add Tag, type Special Handling, press enter

options.label: C
options.text: On the Tag field, select Special Handling from the choice list

options.label: D
options.text: On the Special Handling field, check the box

explanation:
ServiceNow lets users assign a tag from a record form through the form header’s **More options** menu. Select **Add Tag**, enter a new tag name such as `Special Handling`, and press Enter to add it to the record.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Assigning tags](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/washingtondc/platform-user-interface/c_TagAssignment.html)

question: You have been asked to configure a form so that an employee can order a tablet and select the standard accessory options to purchase with it. These standard options are: carrying case, screen cleaner, tablet stand, and screen protector. What approach would you take? (select 3)

options.label: A
options.text: Create Catalog Item for the Tablet, and add a variable set to the form, for the accessory options.

options.label: B
options.text: Create a Record producer, and on the form, add a check box variable for each accessory option.

options.label: C
options.text: On Shopping Cart configuration, select option lo show the Add Accessories button.

options.label: D
options.text: Create one Catalog item for each: tablet, carrying case, screen cleaner, tablet stand, and screen protector.

options.label: E
options.text: Create Catalog Item for the tablet, and on the form, add a check box variable for each accessory option.

explanation:
Standard catalog items support ordering goods and can use variables to capture a requester’s selections. The tablet item can therefore include a reusable variable set or individual checkbox variables for the accessory choices. Alternatively, the tablet and each accessory can be offered as separate catalog items, because items that can be ordered independently are catalog items. Record producers are intended to create task-based records rather than requested items.

**Learn more:** [Service Catalog items](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_IntroductionToCatalogItems.html) · [Service catalog variables](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_ServiceCatalogVariables.html)

question: What do you activate to add applications or functionality to your development instance?
explanation:
ServiceNow plugins are activated to expand the features and functionality available on an instance, including a personal or development instance.

**Learn more:** [Activate a plugin on a personal developer instance](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/activate-plugin-pdi.html)

question: Which utility would you use to orchestrate business processes across services when users have limited technical knowledge?
explanation:
Flow Designer enables process owners to automate business processes without coding, using reusable actions and integrations with other applications and services.

**Learn more:** [Flow Designer](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/flow-designer.html?contentId=rZaEg_PjkgH~nzf8rXjB9g) · [Flow Designer Data Sheet](https://www.servicenow.com/standard/resource-center/data-sheet/ds-flow-designer.html)

question: Which different types of Data Sources can be imported into ServiceNow? (select 4)
explanation:
ServiceNow Import Sets support file-based data from local files or remote network servers, database data accessed through JDBC, and directory data accessed through LDAP. DataHub and an Implementation Spoke are not supported Import Set data-source types.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Data sources](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/integrate-applications/system-import-sets/c_DataSources.html) · [ServiceNow File type data sources](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/integrate-applications/system-import-sets/r_FileTypeDataSource.html)

question: Which field must be set to true on a UI Policy definition record so that the policy applies to all views of the form, rather than just one specific view?
explanation:
On a UI Policy record in ServiceNow, the 'Global' checkbox determines whether the policy applies across every view of the form or is restricted to a single named view. Setting Global to true ensures the UI Policy's conditions and actions take effect regardless of which view a user has open, while leaving it false requires specifying an individual view for the policy to apply to.

**Learn more:** [UI policies - ServiceNow Product Documentation](https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/utah-application-development/page/script/client-scripts/concept/c_UIPolicies.html)

question: Which tab on a knowledge base record would you use to identify the user groups that can read articles in that knowledge base?
explanation:
The **Can Read** related list contains the user criteria that grant users read access to articles in a knowledge base. ServiceNow documents it as the list of user criteria that enables matching users to read knowledge-base articles.

**Learn more:** [Create a knowledge base](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/knowledge-management/create-a-knowledgebase.html) · [Control access at the knowledge base level through user criteria](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/knowledge-management/t_SelectUserCriteria.html)

question:
An IT manager is responsible for the Network and Hardware assignment groups, with 5 team members in each group. These team members are working on many tasks, but the manager cannot view any tasks in the **Service Desk > My Groups Work** list. What could explain this?

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783809260077-zmbajann.png)

options.label: A
options.text: The Service Desk > My Groups Work list shows active work tasks that are not yet assigned.

options.label: B
options.text: The manager does not have the itil role.

options.label: C
options.text: The manager is not a member of the Service Desk group.

options.label: D
options.text: The manager is not a member of the Network and Hardware groups.

options.label: E
options.text: The Assignment Group manager field is empty.

explanation: The **My Groups Work** list displays active tasks assigned to the user’s groups that are still unassigned to an individual. Once a task is assigned to a team member, it no longer appears in that unassigned group-work queue.

question: What are the advantages of assigning work tasks to a group instead of to an individual? (select 4)

options.label: A
options.text: Group members can choose their tasks from My Groups Work

options.label: B
options.text: Groups can assign tasks to users based on on-call schedules

options.label: C
options.text: Site support members can pick tasks, based on Location

options.label: D
options.text: Groups can assign tasks to users based on skills

options.label: E
options.text: Group members can avoid tasks, which are nearing SLA breach

options.label: F
options.text: Groups can assign tasks to users based on availability

explanation:
Assigning work to a group rather than an individual lets group members pick up tasks from My Groups Work (A), and lets the platform route tasks to the right person based on on-call schedules (B), skills (D), and availability (F) through mechanisms like on-call scheduling and Advanced Work Assignment. Option E (letting members avoid tasks nearing an SLA breach) is not a real advantage, and location-based picking (C) is not a standard group-assignment benefit, so availability (F) rather than Location (C) rounds out the four.

**Learn more:** [Advanced Work Assignment (AWA) FAQ](https://www.servicenow.com/community/agent-chat-routing-and-sidebar/advanced-work-assignment-awa-faqs/ta-p/2306792) · [CSA Question 177 - group task assignment](https://cloudtech.how/servicenow/system-administrator-certification-exam/servicenow-csa-question-177/)

question: Which encryption feature is included in ServiceNow by default?
explanation:
ServiceNow provides TLS encryption for data in transit by default. Transparent encryption for data at rest requires additional configuration or subscription options in the standard commercial cloud.

**Learn more:** [Data Encryption on the ServiceNow AI Platform](https://www.servicenow.com/content/dam/servicenow-assets/public/en-us/doc-type/resource-center/white-paper/wp-data-encryption-with-servicenow.pdf)

question: Which items are examples of UI Actions associated with forms? (select 3)
explanation: ServiceNow form UI Actions can be displayed as form buttons, form links, or form context-menu items. Form columns and form views are form layout and display configuration elements rather than UI Action presentation types.

question: Which testing framework is used for testing ServiceNow applications?
explanation:
ServiceNow Automated Test Framework (ATF) is the platform’s native automated-testing capability for validating ServiceNow applications and their functionality.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Automated Test Framework](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/bundle/xanadu-application-development/page/administer/auto-test-framework/concept/automated-test-framework.html)

question: Which module is used for the initial step of importing data?
explanation:
In ServiceNow, a data import starts in the System Import Sets application with the Load Data module (All > System Import Sets > Load Data). On the Load Data form you choose a new or existing import set table, pick the source of the import (for example a file), and submit. The raw rows are then loaded into the import set staging table. Next, a transform map moves the staged rows into the target table, and coalesce fields are defined on that transform map to match existing records. The navigator has no module named Import Data.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Docs (Zurich): Add an import set of alumni for Alumni Center (All > System Import Sets > Load Data)](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/zurich/employee-service-management/alumni-center/asc-add-import-set.html) · [ServiceNow Docs (Zurich): Import sets key concepts](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/zurich/integrate-applications/system-import-sets/c_ImportSetsKeyConcepts.html)

question: Which attributes can be managed through **System Properties > Basic Configuration UI16**? *(select 5)*
explanation:
Basic Configuration UI16 includes properties for the browser tab title (`glide.product.name`), the application navigator’s module text color (`css.$navpage-nav-color-sub`), and the selected base theme (`glide.ui.base_theme.selected_theme`). It does not provide settings for a user’s preferred browser, font style, or animation style. Only three valid options are present in the supplied list, despite the instruction to choose five.

**Learn more:** [Configure logo, colors, and system defaults for Core UI](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/t_ConfigureLogoColorsSysDfltsUI16.html)

question: Which of the following statements most accurately describes the purpose of an Update Set?

options.label: A
options.text: An Update Set allows administrators to group a series of changes into a named set and then move this set as a unit to other systems

options.label: B
options.text: By default, an Update Set includes customizations, Business Rules, and homepages

options.label: C
options.text: An Update Set is a group of customizations that is moved from Production to Development

options.label: D
options.text: By default, the changes included in an Update Set are visible only in the instance to which they are applied

explanation:
An Update Set groups configuration changes into a named, deployable unit that administrators can move to other ServiceNow instances for testing or deployment.

**Learn more:** [System update sets](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/en-US/bundle/yokohama-application-development/page/build/system-update-sets/concept/system-update-sets.html)

question:
A customer asks for the following data-quality measures to be added:

- Incident numbers must be read-only on all lists and forms for every user.
- The Short Description field must be mandatory on all records, across all applications, on Insert.

Which type of policy would meet these requirements?
explanation:
ServiceNow Data Policies enforce mandatory and read-only field states for data entering the system, including UI submissions, imports, web services, and mobile UI. A Data Policy can also be enforced in the browser through its **Use as UI Policy on client** setting, providing consistent field behavior across interfaces.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Data policy](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_DataPolicy.html?contentId=bkk032GHpRWxBckoW_~lZA) · [ServiceNow Data policy fields](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/washingtondc/platform-administration/r_DataPolicyFields.html)

question: Which collaboration tool opens a sidebar and lets you create new conversations with other ServiceNow users?
explanation:
Connect Chat is ServiceNow’s real-time messaging tool for individual and group conversations. Its Connect sidebar lists conversations and provides access to create new ones.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Connect overlay](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/connect/c_CollaborationOverlay.html) · [ServiceNow: Start a direct or group conversation](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/connect/t_StartAConversation.html)

question: Which buttons are commonly used to manage the records in a related list? (select 3)
explanation:
Related lists on a ServiceNow form offer buttons for managing the records linked to the parent record. **New** opens a blank form for the related table. Submitting it creates the record and adds it to the related list. **Edit** opens a slushbucket where existing records can be selected, or removed, and saved to the related list. **Add**, available on some related lists, also associates records with the parent record. There is no standard related-list button named Manage, and Publish is an application workflow action, such as publishing a Knowledge article, rather than a related-list control.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Docs: Select related records](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/bundle/yokohama-platform-user-interface/page/use/using-forms/task/t_SelectRelatedRecords.html) · [ServiceNow Community: Difference between Edit and Add button on related list](https://www.servicenow.com/community/itom-forum/what-is-the-difference-between-edit-and-add-button-on-related/m-p/2933638)

question: Which tables are child tables of the Task table and included with the base system? (select 3)
explanation:
In the ServiceNow base system, Incident [incident], Problem [problem], and Change Request [change_request] extend the Task [task] table. Child tables inherit the Task table’s shared fields and functionality.

**Learn more:** [Table extension and classes](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/table-extension-and-classes.html?contentId=tcFq_LsUEHYP0jZ1YWKwsg)

question: A customer needs to identify and track infrastructure components that support its eCommerce service. Which ServiceNow products could support this requirement? (select 3)
explanation: Discovery identifies infrastructure components, the CMDB records and tracks configuration items and their relationships, and Service Mapping identifies the components and dependencies that support a business or application service such as eCommerce.

question: Which sequence of steps is used to import spreadsheet data into a ServiceNow table?

options.label: B
options.text: Load Data, Create Transform Map, Run Transform

options.label: C
options.text: Define Data Source, Select Transform Map, Run Transform

options.label: D
options.text: Select Import Set, Select Transform Map, Run Transform

explanation: Spreadsheet data is loaded into an import set, mapped to the destination table through a transform map, and then transformed to create or update target-table records.

question: Which ServiceNow products can be used to discover and populate the CMDB? (select 2)
explanation:
ServiceNow Discovery scans networks for attached computers and devices and automatically populates the CMDB with their configuration and status data. IntegrationHub ETL imports, transforms, and integrates third-party source data into selected CMDB classes and attributes.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Populating the CMDB](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/c_OptionsToPopulateCMDB.html) · [ServiceNow: IntegrationHub ETL](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/integration-hub-etl/integrationhub-etl.html)

question: Which ServiceNow utility enables a Service Desk agent to trace from a Service experiencing an issue and identify which CIs supporting that service have active issues?
explanation:
ServiceNow Dependency Views display the CIs that support an application or business service and their relationships. Map indicators show whether a CI has active or pending issues, enabling investigation of the related tasks. [Dependency Views map](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/dependency-views/c_NextGenBSMMaps.html)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Dependency Views map](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/dependency-views/c_NextGenBSMMaps.html)

question: Which feature can categorize a group of records in a list and make them visible to other users?
explanation:
Tags organize records around a shared category or theme. Public tags are shared across the organization and are visible to users who have access to the tagged records.

**Learn more:** [Tag Records | Salesforce Help](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=xcloud.tag_records.htm&language=en_US&type=5)

question: What role do form annotations serve within Table Builder?

options.label: B
options.text: To provide additional information on each field

options.label: C
options.text: To rearrange fields in a form

options.label: D
options.text: To add visual appeal with colors in the designer

explanation: Form annotations provide additional information or context for each field.

question: In the Service Catalog, what do the Create Incident, Password Reset, and Report outage services have in common?

options.label: A
options.text: They direct the user to a record producer

options.label: B
options.text: They direct the user to a catalog property

options.label: C
options.text: They direct the user to a catalog UI policy

options.label: D
options.text: They direct the user to a catalog client script

explanation:
A record producer is a Service Catalog item type that lets end users create task-based records, including incident records, through a catalog-facing experience. The named services therefore direct users to record producers rather than to catalog configuration elements such as properties, UI policies, or client scripts.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Record Producer](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_RecordProducer.html)

question: An IT manager is responsible for the Network and Hardware assignment groups, with 5 team members in each group. The team members are working on many tasks, but the manager cannot view any tasks in the **Service Desk > My Groups Work** list. What could account for this?

options.label: A
options.text: The Assignment Group manager field is empty.

options.label: B
options.text: The manager does not have the itil role.

options.label: C
options.text: The manager is not a member of the Service Desk group.

options.label: D
options.text: The manager is not a member of the Network and Hardware groups.

explanation:
The My Groups Work list displays outstanding work assigned to the logged-in user's groups. Assignment-group management alone does not grant group membership, so a manager who is not a member of the Network and Hardware groups will not see their group tasks there.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Legacy ITIL dashboard](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/yokohama/it-service-management/incident-management/itil-dashboard.html)

question: With the Impersonate role, which type of user can you not impersonate?
explanation:
The ServiceNow Impersonator (`impersonator`) role allows impersonation of users but does not enable impersonation of users who have the `admin` role. A System Administrator is therefore excluded.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Base system roles](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/user-administration/r_BaseSystemRoles.html?contentId=CicEKXNxTK1BP0BaqtAhuw)

question: Which of the following are supported types of client scripts in ServiceNow? (select 4)
explanation:
ServiceNow Client Scripts support the `onLoad`, `onChange`, `onSubmit`, and `onCellEdit` types. These run respectively when a form renders, a field value changes, a form is submitted, or a list cell is edited.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Client scripts](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/scripts/client-scripts.html)

question: Which feature lets you restrict who can contribute to or read knowledge within a knowledge base?
explanation:
ServiceNow User Criteria controls access at the knowledge-base level, including which users may read knowledge articles and which may contribute to them.

**Learn more:** [Control access at the knowledge base level through user criteria](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/knowledge-management/t_SelectUserCriteria.html)

question: What constitutes a role in ServiceNow?

options.label: A
options.text: A role is one record in the Role [user_sys_role] table

options.label: B
options.text: A role is a set of modules for a particular application

options.label: C
options.text: A role is one record in the Role [sys_user_role] table

options.label: D
options.text: A role is a persona used in Live Feed Chat

explanation:
A ServiceNow role is a record in the Roles [sys_user_role] table. Roles grant access to application features and capabilities and can be assigned to users or groups.

**Learn more:** [Exploring user administration](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/user-administration/exploring-user-administration.html)

question: Which option enables the creation of a task-based record from the Service Catalog?
explanation:
A Record Producer is a Service Catalog item that lets end users create task-based records, such as incident records, from the catalog instead of generating a requested item.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Record Producer](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_RecordProducer.html)

question: When testing a catalog item that has a manager-approval flow, which best practices should you follow? (select 3)

options.label: A
options.text: Make sure the latest flows are activated.

options.label: B
options.text: Use the instance Incognito setting to quickly toggle between requester and approver.

options.label: C
options.text: Impersonate the requester to ensure the form works.

options.label: D
options.text: Make sure the requester's user record has a manager specified.

options.label: E
options.text: Create and select your Testing Update Set, before starting the test cases.

options.label: F
options.text: Use your Admin account, so you can approve the items quickly.

explanation: A manager-approval flow must be activated in its current version, and the requester’s user record must have a manager so the approval can be routed. Impersonating the requester validates that the catalog form and request behavior work in the requester’s actual context.

question: What steps are involved in importing data by using an import set?

options.label: A
options.text: Create Import Set; Create transform map; Transform data; Clean up import table

options.label: B
options.text: Create a Transform Map, Load Data, Transform Data, Run Transform Map Script

options.label: C
options.text: Identify source; Import transform map; Run transformer; Verify import

options.label: D
options.text: Select source file; Run AutoMap; Transform data; Clean up target table

explanation:
Importing data with an import set follows a fixed sequence: create the import set by loading source data into a staging (import) table, create a transform map that maps the staging fields to the target table, run the transform to move the data into the target table, then clean up the import set / staging tables. Option A ("Create Import Set; Create transform map; Transform data; Clean up import table") matches this workflow exactly. Option B is wrong because it places "Create a Transform Map" before loading data and ends with "Run Transform Map Script," which is not a defined step in the import-set process.

**Learn more:** [Creating transform maps](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/integrate-applications/system-import-sets/c_CreatingNewTransformMaps.html) · [Importing & transforming external data](https://www.servicenow.com/community/servicenow-ai-platform-articles/administration-importing-amp-transforming-of-external-data/ta-p/2373037)

question: Which table type can be extended by other tables but does not itself extend another table?
explanation:
A base table is an extendable parent table with no parent table of its own. Child tables may extend it and inherit its fields and behavior.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Community: Base versus core tables](https://www.servicenow.com/community/itsm-forum/difference-between-base-table-and-core-table/td-p/629464)

question: What holds the configuration changes made to an instance (for example, changes to a form) and helps implement those changes from the Dev environment into another environment?
explanation:
ServiceNow update sets group and track configuration changes, such as form customizations, so they can be transferred from a development instance to another instance for testing or deployment.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: System update sets](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/system-update-sets/system-update-sets.html) · [ServiceNow: Update set transfers](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/system-update-sets/update-set-transfers.html)

question:
For this implementation, the following tables extend one another:

- The Incident table extends the Task table.
- The Super Incident table extends the Incident table.

In this situation, which table(s) are Parent, Child, and Base tables? (select 5)

options.label: A
options.text: Super Incident table is a Parent table

options.label: B
options.text: Incident table is a Child table

options.label: C
options.text: Super Incident table is a Base table

options.label: D
options.text: Incident table is a Base table

options.label: E
options.text: Task table is a Child table

options.label: F
options.text: Incident table is a Parent table

explanation:
A table that extends another table is a child, and a table can be both a child and a parent when it extends one table while being extended by another. Therefore, Incident is a child of Task and a parent of Super Incident. Task is the base table because it is the parent that does not extend another table; no supplied choice identifies Task as a base table. The available correct choices are consequently limited to B and F.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Table extension and classes](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/table-extension-and-classes.html?contentId=tcFq_LsUEHYP0jZ1YWKwsg)

question: For a Business Rule, the **When** setting specifies when the rule runs. What options are available for defining that timing?
explanation:
The Business Rule **When** setting supports **Before**, **After**, **Async**, and **Display**. These values define whether the rule runs before or after a database operation, asynchronously after it, or when a form is displayed.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Classic Business rules](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/business-rules-classic/c_BusinessRules.html)

question: Which notification methods can be used to alert users when events of concern to them occur? (select 3)
explanation:
ServiceNow supports email notifications, meeting-invitation notifications, and SMS delivery. An email notification can be created as either EMAIL or Meeting Invitation, and recipients subscribed on an SMS channel can receive the notification as an SMS message.

**Learn more:** [Create an email notification](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/t_CreateANotification.html) · [Email and SMS notifications](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_EmailNotifications.html)

question: While viewing a long list of records, you want to quickly filter it so that it displays only records whose Category is Hardware. How could you do this?

options.label: A
options.text: On the Category column header, right click and select Show > Hardware

options.label: B
options.text: Right click on magnifier, type Hardware and click enter

options.label: C
options.text: On the list, locate and right click on the value Hardware, select Show Matching

options.label: D
options.text: On Breadcrumb, click > icon, type Hardware and click enter

options.label: E
options.text: Click Funnel icon, type Hardware and click enter

explanation:
ServiceNow list-field context menus include the quick-filter action **Show Matching**. Selecting it on the value `Hardware` filters the list to records whose Category value matches Hardware.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: List fields](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/r_Fields.html)

question: End-user wait time is based on the round trip between the client and the server. Which activities are included in those round trips?
explanation: A client-server round trip consists of sending a request from the client to the server and receiving the server’s response back at the client.

question: In a filter condition, what is the element called that is based on the table, the user's access rights, and the columns in that table?
explanation:
A condition builder uses a **Field** as the choice list determined by the selected table and the user's access rights. Each field corresponds to data from a column in that table.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Condition builder](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/configure-user-experiences/c_ConditionBuilder.html?contentId=nBDSlmCT8A_m2nVwfM340g) · [ServiceNow: Filters](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/c_Filters.html)

question: On the Form header, which element lets you access form templates?
explanation:
ServiceNow exposes the Template Bar, which provides shortcuts for applying, editing, and creating form templates, from the form header’s **More Options (...)** menu by selecting **Toggle Template Bar**.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow documentation: Toggle the template bar](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/t_ToggleTheTemplateBar.html?contentId=UMatdXi_eEKufIJZ~jk8lQ)

question: Which language is used for scripting in ServiceNow?
explanation:
ServiceNow scripting is based on JavaScript for both client-side and server-side platform customization.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Developer — JavaScript](https://developer.servicenow.com/dev.do#!/learn/learning-plans/xanadu/new_to_servicenow/app_store_learnv2_scripting_xanadu_what_is_javascript)

question: Which options are available in the Data Visualization configuration panel for determining how the data is presented? (select 2)
explanation: Metrics define the quantitative values and aggregations shown in a visualization, while chart mapping determines how those values and fields are assigned to visual elements such as axes, series, or categories. A data source supplies the underlying data but does not itself determine its presentation.

question: Which term most accurately describes something that is created, has work performed on it, and is ultimately moved to a closed state?
explanation: A task is a work item created to track and carry out work. It progresses through its lifecycle as work is performed and is closed when that work is complete.

question: Which area of the ServiceNow UI lets you perform a global search?
explanation:
In ServiceNow Core UI, the Banner frame runs across the top of the page and includes the Global text search icon, which searches records across multiple tables.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Core UI](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/configure-user-experiences/c_UI16.html) · [Global search finds records from multiple tables](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/search-administration/c_GlobalTextSearch.html?contentId=mJylvg9IwIEuot9FYcBTNg)

question: Which of the following statements is true about Service Catalog Items in relation to the Service Catalog?
explanation:
A Service Catalog is composed of discrete catalog items. Each item represents an individually available good, service, request mechanism, or informational offering; therefore, catalog items are the catalog’s building blocks.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Service Catalog items](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_IntroductionToCatalogItems.html)

question: How can you make a list filter accessible to everyone?

options.label: A
options.text: Make active, assign a name, and save

options.label: B
options.text: Assign a group, set visibility, and save

options.label: C
options.text: Assign a name, set visibility, and save

options.label: D
options.text: Make active, set visibility, and save

explanation:
A global list filter is created by giving the filter a name, selecting **Everyone** as its visibility, and saving it. The Everyone setting makes the filter available to all users.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Save and use filters in a list view](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/t_SavingFilters.html?contentId=ziSqngNym_DXUq_8EGaUpQ)

question: Which module is used to access the knowledge bases available to you?
explanation:
The ServiceNow Knowledge Management homepage displays knowledge content organized by knowledge base and category, and it is accessed through **Self-Service > Knowledge**. The **Knowledge Bases** navigation is used to administer knowledge-base records, not the standard user-facing knowledge homepage.

**Learn more:** [Using the homepage of Knowledge Management v3](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/knowledge-management/c_KnowledgeHomepage.html?contentId=bx3KyGhdG4E7KkBKAv2d5w)

question: What are the primary components of the Form Design interface? (select 3)
explanation:
The Form Design interface consists of the page header, which identifies the current table and view; the field navigator, which manages fields; and the form layout, which displays the form’s fields and other elements.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Form designer documentation](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_FormDesign.html)

question: Which benefits are provided by building flows with Flow Designer? (select 3)

options.label: B
options.text: Provides built-in libraries /API for complex coding

options.label: D
options.text: Provides natural-language descriptions of flow logic

options.label: F
options.text: Supports easy integration with 3rd party systems

explanation:
Flow Designer provides a natural-language, no-code environment for creating and automating digital workflows. With IntegrationHub, flows can also integrate third-party services and systems. These capabilities support understandable flow logic, no-code development, and external-system integration.

**Learn more:** [Flow Designer Data Sheet — ServiceNow](https://www.servicenow.com/standard/resource-center/data-sheet/ds-flow-designer.html)

question: Tables can be configured with many-to-many relationships. What is a classic example of a scenario in which the tables would have a many-to-many relationship?

options.label: A
options.text: Vendors can sell multiple products; and products can be sold by multiple vendors.

options.label: B
options.text: A Task can trigger many Workflows; and a Workflow can trigger many Tasks.

options.label: C
options.text: Requests can contain many Items; and Items can be any item from the catalog.

options.label: D
options.text: A Configuration Item can belong to multiple Classes, and Classes can contain multiple Configuration Items.

explanation: A vendor can sell multiple products, while a product can be offered by multiple vendors. This is a many-to-many relationship and is normally represented using an intermediary junction table.

question:
Which icon would you double-click to expand or collapse the list of all Applications and Modules?

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783808803127-cu3g62gc.jpg)
explanation:
The Application (All applications tab) icon controls the display of the application menus and their modules. Double-clicking it expands or collapses all applications in the navigator.

**Learn more:** [Use the Core UI navigator](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/ui16-navigator-tasks.html)

question: The Employee Onboarding team has requested a way for managers to order computers, monitors, business cards, and cell phones for newly hired employees. How would you meet this requirement?
explanation:
An Order Guide groups multiple related Service Catalog items into one request. It is intended for bundled needs such as new-employee onboarding and can pass shared information to the individual ordered items.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Order guides](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_ServiceCatalogOrderGuides.html) · [ServiceNow: Service Catalog items](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_IntroductionToCatalogItems.html)

question: Which ServiceNow feature can be triggered by events and is used to notify users about activities or updates in ServiceNow?
explanation: ServiceNow Notifications can be triggered by events and deliver information to users about activities or updates.

question: Which tables are available by default in a ServiceNow instance? (select 3)
explanation: ServiceNow includes the User table for user records, the Incident table for incident-management records, and the Task table as a foundational table extended by many task-based applications. The other listed names are not default core tables under those names.

question: Which of the following statements applies when a set of fields is coalesced during an import?

options.label: A
options.text: If a match is found using the coalesce fields, the existing record is updated with the information being imported

options.label: B
options.text: If a match is not found using the coalesce fields, the system does not create a Transform Map

options.label: C
options.text: If a match is found using the coalesce fields, the system creates a new record

options.label: D
options.text: If a match is not found using the coalesce fields, the existing record is updated with the information being imported

explanation:
Coalesce fields are used to find an existing target-table record during an import transformation. When the coalesce values match an existing record, that record is updated with the imported data; if no match is found, a new record is created.

**Learn more:** [Updating records using coalesce](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/integrate-applications/system-import-sets/c_ImportSetCoalesce.html)

question: Which ServiceNow feature lets you include data from a secondary, related table in a report?
explanation:
Dot-walking accesses fields through a reference relationship, allowing reports to use fields from extended or related tables. ServiceNow documentation states that dot-walking provides access to fields on related tables for reporting.

**Learn more:** [Report on extended tables](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/reporting/t_AccessFieldExtendedTable.html)

question: Which feature helps define rules that restrict users’ permissions to view and interact with data?
explanation: Access control rules enforce authorization by defining which users can access data and what interactions they are permitted to perform.

question: Which action allows a user to view and set date and time formats in their instance?

options.label: A
options.text: Select the User menu > Preferences > Time Settings > Toggle display time zone

options.label: B
options.text: Ask the user to adjust the time zone on their personal computer

options.label: C
options.text: Use the system properties to correct the instance's time zone

options.label: D
options.text: Select the User menu > Preferences > Language & Region > Set date and time format and time zone

options.label: E
options.text: Create a UI Script to set the default timezone

explanation:
ServiceNow’s User Menu > Preferences > Language & Region settings let users configure regional display preferences, including date/time-related formatting and the session time zone. System properties establish global defaults, not an individual user’s preference settings.

**Learn more:** [Configure Next Experience language and region preferences](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/next-experience-language-preferences.html?contentId=Is_pAULEi7aZoIAJwFdhvA)

question: As an administrator, what must you do to access the features of High Security Settings?

options.label: C
options.text: Add security_admin role to your user account

options.label: D
options.text: Use System Administration > Elevate Roles module

explanation:
High Security Settings features require the elevated security_admin privilege. The base system administrator obtains that session-based privilege by selecting **Elevate Roles** and elevating the role; the elevation ends when the session ends.

**Learn more:** [Elevate to a privileged role](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/t_ElevateToAPrivilegedRole.html) · [Elevated privilege roles](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/c_ElevatedPrivilege.html)

question: Which of the following safeguards applications by identifying and limiting access to available files and data?
explanation:
Application scope protects applications by identifying and restricting access to an application's files and data. Each scoped application has its own namespace, and other applications can reach its tables, scripts and other resources only where cross-scope access is explicitly permitted. Access control rules, by contrast, secure individual tables, fields and records through role and condition checks.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Docs: Application scope](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/application-development/c_ApplicationScope.html)

question: While using the CMDB, what is the name for the component that must be managed to deliver services?
explanation: A Configuration Item (CI) is a component that must be managed in order to provide a service and is recorded in the CMDB.

question: A company is recognizing all first-line workers with a special T-shirt for their hard work. The management team needs employees to be able to order the T-shirt and specify their preferred size and color. How would you ensure that only first-line workers (non-managers) can submit the order?

options.label: A
options.text: Create Record Producer and use the Available For list to specify First Line [sn_first_line] role

options.label: B
options.text: Create Catalog Item and use the Not Available list to specify the Manager Group

options.label: C
options.text: Create Catalog Item and use the Available For list to specify ITIL [itil] role

options.label: D
options.text: Create Order Guide and use the User Criteria list to specify First Line [sn_first_line] role

explanation:
A catalog item is appropriate for requesting a T-shirt with selectable variables such as size and color. Applying the Manager Group as a Not Available user criterion prevents members of that group from accessing the item; Not Available criteria override availability, thereby excluding managers from submitting the request.

**Learn more:** [Apply user criteria to items and categories](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/t_AppUserCritItemsCat.html)

question: Which administrator role is required to modify High Security Settings?
explanation:
The `security_admin` role is the elevated-privilege role that authorizes changes to High Security Settings. The `admin` role alone can view those properties but must elevate to `security_admin` to modify them.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Security_admin role](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/security-admin-role.html) · [ServiceNow: Exploring High Security Settings](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/exploring-high-security-settings.html)

question: In a filter condition, which component is invariably a choice list?
explanation:
In ServiceNow’s condition builder, the operator is a choice list whose available entries depend on the selected field type. A value may be either a text-entry field or a choice list, so it is not invariably a choice list.

**Learn more:** [Create a condition statement using the condition builder](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/create-cond-state-using-cond-build.html)

question: A user reports seeing a blank page after selecting **Create New** in your custom Inventory application. You have verified that they can view the Inventory application and its **Create New** module in the application navigator. What could be causing this issue?

options.label: A
options.text: Create New module has a broken link

options.label: C
options.text: User should be using Chrome instead of Explorer for their browser

options.label: D
options.text: User has read role, but not the write role on the Inventory table

explanation:
Read access permits viewing records, whereas write access permits updating records; access controls also govern record-creation operations. A user who has only the read role for the Inventory table lacks the authorization needed to create or edit Inventory records, which can prevent the new-record form from loading or being usable.

**Learn more:** [ACL types](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/access-control/acl-rule-types.html) · [Explore Access Control Lists](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/access-control/exploring-access-control-list.html)

question: Where can administrators check which release is running on a ServiceNow instance?
explanation: The **Stats** module shows the instance build information, including the build name that identifies the ServiceNow release currently running.

question: While working on a task, which field should you use to share knowledge and other details that are visible to the customer?
explanation:
Additional comments is the task-record journal field used to communicate customer-visible information and updates; entries are recorded in the task activity.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Important Task table fields](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/r_ImportantTaskTableFields.html?contentId=loq~GAl027VPDvDQhjZ4Fg)

question: Which section of a task record would you use to view the latest update made to that record?
explanation:
The Activity section on ServiceNow Task records displays the record’s activity history and receives updates in real time, allowing users to see the latest record information.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Activity formatter](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_ActivityFormatter.html?contentId=9boopYAo82XdoITQuZTUAA)

question: Security rules are established to limit users’ permissions to view and interact with data. What are these security rules called?
explanation:
Access control rules, implemented as access control list (ACL) rules, restrict access to data by requiring users to meet defined requirements before they can interact with it.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Access Control List Rules](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/access-control/access-control-rules.html)

question: What lets you trace the relationship from an infrastructure item, such as a Server, to the Services that depend on that Server?
explanation:
CMDB relationships store typed links between configuration items and enable dependency traversal across infrastructure and service CIs. A relationship can therefore connect a Server, directly or indirectly, to Services that depend on it.

**Learn more:** [CI relationships in the CMDB](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/c_CIRelationships.html?contentId=~TP_PO7BT1X~BDLhGrZpaA)

question: On the knowledge base record, which tab do you use to specify which users can write articles for the knowledge base?
explanation:
The **Can Contribute** tab grants contribute access, allowing users who meet its criteria to create and modify knowledge articles in the knowledge base.

**Learn more:** [Create a knowledge base](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/knowledge-management/create-a-knowledgebase.html) · [Managing access to knowledge bases and knowledge articles](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/knowledge-management/user-access-knowledge.html)

question: You have learned about a newly released ServiceNow application and want to try it to determine whether it could be useful for your company’s ServiceNow implementation. What is the best way to gain hands-on experience with the new application?

options.label: A
options.text: Search the wiki for the sales demo request form

options.label: B
options.text: Check the latest release notes at docs servicenow.com

options.label: C
options.text: Activate the application plug in, on your personal dev instance

options.label: D
options.text: Activate the application plug in, on your company's production instance.

explanation:
A personal developer instance provides a sandbox for learning, exploring, and testing applications without affecting a customer or production instance. ServiceNow specifically recommends testing a plugin on a PDI before it is launched in production.

**Learn more:** [Activate a plugin on a personal developer instance](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/activate-plugin-pdi.html) · [Personal developer instance guide](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/personal_developer_instance_guide.html)

question: The Report Designer includes several sections for configuring a report. Which section is used to change the report’s appearance, including colors, titles, and legend layout?
explanation:
The Style section controls a report’s visual presentation, including its colors, title-related display settings, and legend options.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Chart colors](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/en-US/bundle/zurich-now-intelligence/page/use/reporting/concept/c_ChartColors.html) · [ServiceNow: Color palettes](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/reporting/color-palettes.html)

question: While presenting a customer with their Incident form, they ask that the Priority field title be changed to display their internal terminology, PValue. How would you accomplish this? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Right click on Priority and select Configure Label

options.label: B
options.text: Right click on Priority and select Configure Dictionary

options.label: C
options.text: Right click on Priority and select Configure Display Settings

options.label: D
options.text: Right click on Priority and select Configure Column

explanation:
ServiceNow field labels can be changed by right-clicking the field label and choosing Configure Label. The same result can be made through Configure Dictionary by updating the dictionary entry’s Column label, which controls the label shown on form fields and list headers.

**Learn more:** [Change the field label or hint](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/t_ChangeFieldLabelOrHint.html) · [Dictionary entry form](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/r_DictionaryEntryForm.html)

question: Roles can inherit permissions from other roles. Which role inherits all permissions of the catalog role and the user_criteria_admin role, while also having permission to create Items and Services?
explanation: The catalog_admin role includes the inherited permissions of both the catalog and user_criteria_admin roles, and it grants administrative capabilities to create and manage catalog items and services.

question: Tables can have one-to-many relationships. In the Service Catalog, which are examples of tables with one-to-many relationships? (select 3)

options.label: A
options.text: One Approval can have many Requests

options.label: B
options.text: One Request can have many Requested Items

options.label: C
options.text: One Requested Item can have many Approvals

options.label: D
options.text: One Requested Item can have many Catalog Tasks

options.label: E
options.text: One Cart can have many Requests

explanation:
A single Request can include multiple Requested Items. A Requested Item can have multiple required approvers and can generate multiple Catalog Tasks as part of its fulfillment process.

**Learn more:** [Service Catalog request screens](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_RequestingAServiceCatalogItem.html) · [Define an item approval](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/washingtondc/build-workflows/t_DefineAnItemApproval.html)

question: When a user reports being unable to see modules in the Application Navigator, what can you do to determine which modules are visible to that user?

options.label: A
options.text: Look up their password, so you can login with their account

explanation:
Impersonation runs the session with the selected user’s access and displays the same menus and modules available to that user, allowing an authorized administrator to verify the user’s Application Navigator visibility.

**Learn more:** [Impersonating users](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/user-administration/c_ImpersonateAUser.html)

question: Which ServiceNow resource provides a framework that ensures the data required by your ServiceNow application maps correctly to the appropriate CMDB tables?
explanation:
The Common Service Data Model (CSDM) provides the standards for defining configuration items and their relationships so that application data is placed in the appropriate CMDB tables.

**Learn more:** [Common Service Data Model (CSDM)](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/common-service-data-model-csdm/csdm-landing-page.html) · [Mapping data to CMDB tables](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/common-service-data-model-csdm/csdm-to-cmdb-mapping.html)

question: Which components fall under the customer’s responsibility in the Shared Responsibility Model? (select 2)
explanation:
Under ServiceNow’s Shared Responsibility Model, the customer is responsible for controlling user access through authentication and authorization and for protecting its data with encryption at rest. ServiceNow is responsible for the underlying infrastructure, media disposal and destruction, and backup and restore.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow — Safeguarding your data](https://www.servicenow.com/content/dam/servicenow-assets/public/en-us/doc-type/resource-center/ebook/safeguarding-your-data.pdf)

question:
Some cables use a prefix, such as `x_`.

What type of table has a name beginning with this prefix?
explanation:
In ServiceNow, scoped applications use a namespace identifier beginning with `x_`, and tables in those applications are prefixed with that identifier. [ServiceNow: Namespace identifier](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/c_NamespaceIdentifier.html)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Namespace identifier](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/c_NamespaceIdentifier.html) · [ServiceNow: Create a table](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/t_CreateATable.html?contentId=8EfyhC9ilIfGGhbCb3bm0Q)

question:
A customer requests the following changes to a form:

1. When the Caller field is populated, automatically look up the caller's location and load it into the Location field.
2. Add a notice at the top of the page when the record is submitted.

What type of script would you use to fulfill this requirement?
explanation:
ServiceNow client scripts run in response to form events. An onChange client script can react to the Caller field being populated and set the Location field, while an onSubmit client script runs when the form is submitted and can add a form message at the top of the page.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Client scripts](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/scripts/client-scripts.html?contentId=6S3mbRkaNeuGk3PoOybSxQ) · [ServiceNow Scripting](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/scripts/c_Script.html)

question: Where do UI Policies execute?
explanation: ServiceNow UI Policies execute on the client side in the browser, where they dynamically control form-field behavior.

question: Which table serves as the base table for the Configuration Management Database hierarchy?
explanation:
The Base Configuration Item table, `cmdb`, is the root table in the ServiceNow CMDB inheritance hierarchy. The Configuration Item table, `cmdb_ci`, extends `cmdb`; CI-specific classes extend from that structure. [Configuration Item [cmdb_ci] class](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/cmdb-table-property-descriptions.html?contentId=b7EatfVVObXRwbFPYx6uDw)

**Learn more:** [Configuration Item cmdb_ci class](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/cmdb-table-property-descriptions.html?contentId=b7EatfVVObXRwbFPYx6uDw)

question: Which module in the Service Catalog application does an Administrator open to start creating a new item?
explanation: The Service Catalog **Maintain Items** module is the administrative entry point for creating and managing catalog items.

question: Which application is primarily used to load data into ServiceNow?
explanation:
System Import Sets is the ServiceNow application for importing data from external sources into import-set staging tables and mapping it to ServiceNow tables through transform maps.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Import sets](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/integrate-applications/system-import-sets/import-sets-landing-page.html) · [ServiceNow Run an import](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/integrate-applications/system-import-sets/t_RunImport.html)

question: Which field type is Boolean and is displayed as a check box?
explanation:
In ServiceNow the Boolean field type is labelled **True/False**. It stores 1 or 0 and is displayed on forms as a check box (checked = true, unchecked = false), and as true/false in lists. Yes/No, On/Off, Binary and 0/1 are not field type names.

**Learn more:** [True/False (Boolean) field behavior in ServiceNow with null values](https://www.servicenow.com/community/servicenow-ai-platform-blog/true-false-boolean-field-behavior-in-servicenow-with-null-values/ba-p/2291273) · [ServiceNow Field Types and Dictionary Entries Explained](https://s2-labs.com/servicenow-admin/servicenow-field-types)

question:
A customer requests the following changes to a form:

- Make **Resolution code** mandatory when the state changes to **Resolved**.
- Hide the **Major Incident** check box unless the logged-in user has the **Major Incident Manager** role.

Which type of rule(s) would you use to implement these requirements?
explanation:
ServiceNow UI Policies control conditional form behavior at runtime. Their actions can set a field as mandatory or hidden, and a role-based script or condition can limit visibility of the Major Incident check box to Major Incident Managers.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow UI policies](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/t_CreateAUIPolicy.html)

question: Knowledge Base Search results may be sorted by which of the following? (select 3)
explanation:
Knowledge Base Search supports sorting knowledge content by relevancy, most recent update, or number of views.

**Learn more:** [Search using Knowledge Management v3](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/knowledge-management/r_KnowledgeSearch.html)

question: Which types of interfaces are included with the ServiceNow platform? (select 3)
explanation:
ServiceNow provides web-based Now Platform user interfaces, mobile experiences through Now Mobile Apps, and self-service experiences through Service Portals. Agent Control Center, Back Office Dashboard, and Field Service Taskboard are not platform-wide interface types.

**Learn more:** [Configure UIs and portals](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/configure-uis-and-portals.html) · [Now Mobile app](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/mobile/now-mobile-app.html)

question: Which element tracks items that are not saved in a field on a record?
explanation: The Activity formatter captures and displays record activity, including information such as work notes, comments, approvals, and changes that is not stored as a standard record field.

question: Which action opens the Form Design interface?

options.label: A
options.text: In the Form context menu, select Configure > Form Design

options.label: B
options.text: In the Form context menu, select Configure > Form Layout > Designer

options.label: C
options.text: In the Form context menu, select User Experience > UX Dashboard

options.label: D
options.text: In the Form context menu, select Configure > Forms > Developer

options.label: E
options.text: In the form context menu, select Pages > Page Design

explanation:
In ServiceNow Core UI, Form Designer is launched from an existing form’s context menu by selecting **Configure > Form Design**. [ServiceNow: Form designer](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_FormDesign.html?contentId=Lmx4jo9HzEd0aVLwaTjssA)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Form designer](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_FormDesign.html?contentId=Lmx4jo9HzEd0aVLwaTjssA)

question: Which statement accurately describes the differences between a Client Script and a Business Rule?

options.label: A
options.text: A Client Script executes before a record is loaded and a Business Rule executes after a record is loaded

options.label: B
options.text: A Client Script executes on the server and a Business Rule executes on the client

options.label: C
options.text: A Client Script executes on the client and a Business Rule executes on the server

options.label: D
options.text: A Client Script executes before a record is loaded and a Business Rule executes after a record is updated

explanation:
In ServiceNow, Client Scripts run in the client web browser for form-related events, whereas Business Rules run on the server when applicable record or table operations occur.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Client scripts](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/scripts/client-scripts.html) · [ServiceNow: Classic Business rules](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/business-rules-classic/c_BusinessRules.html)

question: Where do you navigate to add a list of Incidents that a user created to the bottom of that user’s record?

options.label: B
options.text: Right-click on Form > Configure > Related Cases

options.label: D
options.text: Right-click on the Form > Configure > Add Lists

explanation: ServiceNow form related lists are managed from the form context menu under **Configure > Related Lists**. This is where an Incidents list can be added to a user record.

question: Which banner icon is used to modify your personal system settings, such as your instance color scheme?
explanation: The gear icon opens personal system settings, including appearance preferences such as the instance color scheme.

question: What is the definition of a group?

options.label: A
options.text: A collection of subject matter experts

explanation: A group is a collection of users, typically used to organize users and assign shared access or permissions.

question:
ServiceNow includes a resource that provides the following:

- A common, standardized set of service-related definitions across ServiceNow products and the platform, enabling and supporting true service-level reporting.
- A CMDB framework across the products and platform, enabling and supporting multiple configuration strategies.

Which resource do these statements describe?
explanation: The Common Services Data Model (CSDM) establishes shared definitions for services and a consistent CMDB data-modeling framework across ServiceNow. This supports reliable service-level reporting while allowing multiple configuration-management strategies.

question: Which path in the Filter Navigator displays the record list from the `sys_user` table?
explanation:
